title: Raise the Python floor to 3.11 — StrEnum already requires it and 3.10 is unsupported in practice
description:
src/seeds/models.py:12 does 'from enum import Enum, StrEnum'. enum.StrEnum was added in Python 3.11, but pyproject declares requires-python = '>=3.10' and the CI matrix tests ['3.10','3.11','3.12','3.13']. On 3.10 that is an ImportError at startup — every command, not a type warning. Nothing caught it because the change (15d3a6c, opening the seed_type vocabulary) has not been pushed.

It also shows up locally as a red pre-push gate: 'uv run mypy src/' reports 11 errors in 6 files, all cascading from models.py:12 as '"str" has no attribute "value"', because StrEnum resolves to Any at mypy's configured python_version = '3.10'.

## Why raise the floor rather than change the code

3.10 was never a chosen target. 1270e68 (2026-07-16) raised it from >=3.9 purely because a Dependabot bump to mypy>=2.3.0 made the dev deps unsatisfiable and broke 'uv lock'; before that, >=3.9 was uv init's default at project creation (812e9f8). No user asked for 3.10.

That same commit records the project's policy: '\''Python 3.9 reached end-of-life in Oct 2025, so drop it.'\'' Python 3.10 reaches EOL in October 2026 — roughly six weeks from this bead. Applying the existing rule drops it.

3.11 is the floor the code actually requires. Going further to 3.13 (which CLAUDE.md currently claims) would cut 3.11 and 3.12 for no technical reason.

## Docs already disagree and must be reconciled

pyproject says >=3.10, README says 3.10+, CLAUDE.md says 'Python 3.13+'. Two of the three are wrong whatever floor is chosen.
design:
Raise the floor; do NOT rewrite SeedType.

- pyproject.toml: requires-python '>=3.10' -> '>=3.11'; [tool.mypy] python_version '3.10' -> '3.11'; drop the 3.10 Programming Language classifier if present.
- .github/workflows/ci.yml: drop '3.10' from the python-version matrix.
- README: '3.10+' -> '3.11+'.
- CLAUDE.md: 'Python 3.13+' -> 'Python 3.11+' (currently wrong in the other direction).
- Regenerate uv.lock if the floor change moves any resolution.
- src/seeds/models.py is NOT edited. StrEnum stays; it becomes legal once the declared floor matches what it needs.

The alternative considered and rejected: 'class SeedType(str, Enum)' would work on 3.10 and satisfy mypy, and all SeedType uses go through .value explicitly so it is behaviourally safe here. Rejected because it preserves support for a version nobody chose and that is weeks from EOL, at the cost of a construct the author did not reach for.
acceptance_criteria: 'uv run mypy src/' exits 0 with no errors — all 11 resolve from the config change alone, with no edit to models.py. 'uv run pytest' still passes (714 tests at time of filing). pyproject, README and CLAUDE.md all state 3.11 consistently. The CI matrix no longer contains 3.10. uv.lock is regenerated if the floor change affects resolution, and 'uv lock --check' is clean.
notes: Also raised two surfaces the bead did not name, both required for the floor to be real. (1) pyproject [tool.ruff] target-version py310 -> py311; left at py310 it contradicts the acceptance criterion that pyproject state 3.11 consistently. Consequence: UP017 datetime-timezone-utc fired 51 times and was autofixed mechanically to datetime.UTC across src/seeds/models.py, src/seeds/export.py and tests/ -- purely timezone.utc -> UTC plus matching import rewrites, no logic changed. Rejected alternative: pin ruff at py310 or ignore UP017, i.e. keep the linter on a version nobody supports. (2) .pre-commit-config.yaml pytest-matrix-pre-push looped for v in 3.10 3.11 3.12; unchanged, the pre-push gate would keep running the suite on 3.10 and failing on the StrEnum ImportError forever. Now 3.11 3.12, with the surrounding comment updated. .python-version (3.13) left alone -- it pins the local dev interpreter, above the floor, not an assertion of it. models.py StrEnum untouched as specced; mypy went 11 errors -> 0 from the config change alone.
close_reason: Raised requires-python to >=3.11; mypy 11 errors -> 0 with StrEnum untouched, 714 tests pass

title: the differential harness cannot observe 0.6 on mani: seeds 0.6 itself cannot read a store predating the relationships table
description:
Found while fixing bead seeds-4co.26 (the converter crash on mani), 2026-09-01.

seeds convert now handles mani correctly: 14 seeds converted, round-trip
verified, prefix 'seed' derived from the ids, and both absent tables
(relationships, config) named in the report.

But `just differential ~/projects/outins/mani` still REFUSES, now for a
different reason. The refusal moved off the converter and onto the BASELINE:

  REFUSED  mani: 0.6 'sync --flush-only' failed: ...
           sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: relationships
           (v0.6.0/src/seeds/db.py:682, in get_relationships)

seeds v0.6.0 cannot read this store either. Its SeedsDatabase._get_conn runs
only the resolution and config COLUMN migrations; it never runs the schema
script, so the relationships table is never created on an old store. v0.6.0
DOES ship a migrate_to_relationships() that would create and populate the
table from `related_to` and the legacy `questions` table -- but it is DEAD
CODE: `git grep migrate_to_relationships v0.6.0 -- src` finds only the
definition. Nothing calls it.

So mani was orphaned under 0.6 long before 0.7 existed. That is also why it has
no .seeds/seeds.jsonl beside its db: 0.6 could never write one for it.

The consequence for the harness is that its premise -- compare 0.6 behaviour
with 0.7's -- is VACUOUS on this store, the way it is on the two empty stores
(agent_assessor, beads), which the anti-vacuity guard already refuses on
purpose. Today mani lands in the generic refusal bucket with a 30-line
traceback, which reads like a defect in the current code rather than a fact
about 0.6.

NEEDS A RULING, which is why this is filed rather than fixed. Making
`just differential ~/projects/outins/mani` "run to completion" means giving the
harness a new mode for "0.6 cannot read this store at all", and deciding what
it then asserts instead (conversion clean? check clean? all 14 ids present in
the tree?). That is a decision about what the safety net proves, not a bug fix,
and there is more than one defensible shape for it. Options seen so far:

  a. Leave it refusing, but recognise the 0.6-unreadable case explicitly and
     print a one-line reason instead of a traceback -- the same treatment the
     empty stores get.
  b. Add a convert-only mode: no 0.6 arm, assert the conversion verified and
     `seeds check` is clean, and say plainly that no comparison was made.
  c. Something else.

Source: bead seeds-4co.26
acceptance_criteria: just differential ~/projects/outins/mani ends in a named, one-line outcome rather than a 30-line 0.6 traceback, and the record says whether 0.7's conversion of mani was verified. Whatever shape is chosen, the two empty stores (agent_assessor, beads) keep refusing as they do now.
notes:
RULED (@aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01): keep refusing, but distinguish WHY. The harness must separate "seeds 0.6 cannot read this store" from "seeds convert crashed" - the operator should learn the repo was already orphaned under 0.6, not conclude that 0.7 broke it.

Confirmed independently before ruling: seeds v0.6.0 dies on mani with the identical sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: relationships, raised from its own db.py. v0.6.0 does ship migrate_to_relationships() which would have created and populated the table from the legacy related_to column, and it is dead code - only its definition appears in the v0.6.0 tree. mani was orphaned under 0.6 long before 0.7 existed, which is also why it carries no seeds.jsonl.

Rejected: falling back to convert-and-check-only, which proves something but not what the harness claims to prove, and would need the report to carefully say which weaker assertion it made. Rejected: reviving 0.6 dead migration code against a copy to manufacture a baseline - most faithful in principle, but it means executing a code path nobody has ever run on real data in order to test a migration, which is a worse risk than the gap it closes.

The refusal text should carry what IS known, since it is not nothing: 0.7 converts mani cleanly - 14 seeds, round-trip verified, seeds check clean - it is only the COMPARISON that is impossible. Nothing claimed that was not proved.

Note the anti-vacuity guard already has two refusal reasons (empty corpus, convert crashed); this is a third, and they should read as distinct causes rather than one bucket.

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-01 on branch seeds-4co.27/harness-baseline-refusals.

Design pick (2-way, code only): the three causes are separated by a REQUIRED
keyword-only `reason` slug on Refusal, drawn from a documented REFUSAL_REASONS
table, rather than by wording alone. Wording drifts and cannot be gated; a slug
can. Two AST tests in tests/test_differential_harness.py close it in both
directions -- every `Refusal(..., reason=...)` must cite a described slug, and
every described slug must be raised somewhere -- mirroring the ALLOWLIST
discipline already in the file. Eight reasons in all: not-a-store,
already-converted, convert-crashed, no-0.6-baseline, 0.6-command-failed,
0.7-command-failed, empty-corpus, harness-broken.

Design pick (2-way, code only): the 0.6-unreadable case is detected by a pure
classifier `missing_legacy_table(stderr)` matching an ANCHORED
`^sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: (\w+)$`, not by hard-coding
'relationships'. Any table 0.6 requires and the store predates is the same fact
about the store; the anchor is what keeps a seed body quoting the phrase (this
harness echoes bodies) from being read as a 0.6 crash. `last_error_line()` also
replaces the raw traceback in the remaining 0.6/0.7 command-failure refusals.

Verified over all fourteen repos with a store in one run: 11 pass with 0
regressions, 3 refuse across 2 causes, exit 2 (correct, not red). mani now
reads: "[no-0.6-baseline] ... seeds 0.6 (v0.6.0) cannot read this store either
-- its own db.py raises 'no such table: relationships' ... 0.7 does read it: 14
seed(s) converted, 14 round-trip verified, check clean". The third cause,
convert-crashed, is defined and no longer fires -- seeds-4co.26 fixed it.
close_reason: the harness names its refusal causes from a documented REFUSAL_REASONS table gated by AST tests in both directions; mani now refuses as [no-0.6-baseline] explaining that 0.6 cannot read the store either and that 0.7 converts it cleanly, rather than emitting a 0.6 traceback that implies 0.7 broke it

title: seeds convert crashes with a raw OperationalError on a legacy store predating the relationships table
description:
Found by the differential harness on 2026-09-01, running against all remaining repos.

  REFUSED  mani: seeds convert CRASHED on this store, so 0.7 behaviour cannot
           be observed at all: OperationalError: no such table: relationships

mani/.seeds/seeds.db holds only the tables `seeds` (14 rows) and `questions` (0 rows). There is NO relationships table, and no seeds.jsonl beside it. That is a schema predating relationships entirely - an older store than any this epic has handled.

seeds.legacy queries relationships unconditionally, so the operator gets a bare sqlite3.OperationalError.

THIS IS THE SAME SHAPE AS THE ANSWERS BUG (bead seeds-4co.24), one layer down: a legacy store older than an assumption baked into the reader, surfacing as a raw traceback rather than a named diagnostic. That bug was about an unexpected VALUE in a column; this is an absent TABLE. The fix should generalise rather than special-casing relationships - a legacy store is whatever schema it happens to be, and the reader should say which table it wanted and could not find.

RULING NEEDED on one point, which is why this is filed rather than fixed: is a missing relationships table simply "no relationships" (convert with an empty edge set), or evidence the store is too old to convert safely and should be refused with an explanation? 14 seeds are at stake in the only known instance. My read is the former - the seeds themselves are intact and readable, and refusing would strand them over a table that carries nothing.

Reproduce: just differential ~/projects/outins/mani

Source: bead seeds-4co.17, bead seeds-4co.24
acceptance_criteria: A legacy SQLite store with no 'relationships' table converts, treating its relationship set as empty. 'just differential ~/projects/outins/mani' runs to completion instead of refusing. Any other missing legacy table produces a ConversionError naming the store and the table, never a bare sqlite3 error. A fixture pins the no-relationships-table shape.
notes:
DESIGN PICKS (code-only 2-way choices, ruled per the ambiguity rubric):

1. REQUIRED vs OPTIONAL tables. seeds.legacy now declares REQUIRED_TABLES =
   {seeds} and OPTIONAL_TABLES = {relationships, questions, config}. The test is
   not "does the reader touch it" but "does it carry deliberation": only `seeds`
   holds ids, titles and bodies, so its absence means there is nothing to
   convert. relationships carries edges BETWEEN seeds, questions is debris the
   converter drops wholesale anyway, and config carries one string the converter
   already derives from the ids when missing. The schema is checked once, when
   the read-only connection opens, so a store too old to convert says so before
   it half-converts and says it the same way whichever method was called first.

2. Absent optional tables are REPORTED, not passed over silently -- and all of
   them, not just relationships. Reporting only relationships would be the
   special-case the bead forbids; the uniform rule costs one extra line on
   stores that never had a `questions` table, on a one-time migration report.

3. _load_db now returns a _DbLoad record instead of a 4-tuple, because the
   fourth and fifth values are both "what was not read" and positional
   unpacking made which-is-which a matter of counting commas.

MEASURED 2026-09-01, read-only, across all 15 legacy stores on titan:
mani and beads are the only two on the pre-relationships schema (seeds +
questions only, no config, no seeds.jsonl). Edges lived in a `related_to` JSON
column there; across all 15 stores it holds 100 rows and ZERO whose two ends
both still exist (all 100 are in this repo's own store and name ids from a
retired `seed-` prefix). So no absent table anywhere hides an edge, and the
ruling loses nothing.

NEW DEFECT FOUND, needs a ruling (NOT fixed here): `just differential
~/projects/outins/mani` still REFUSES, but for a different reason. seeds
convert now succeeds; the refusal moved to the 0.6 baseline, which cannot read
this store either -- `seeds 0.6 sync --flush-only` dies in v0.6.0's own db.py
with the same `no such table: relationships`. v0.6.0 HAS a
`migrate_to_relationships()` that would have created and populated the table,
but it is dead code: nothing in v0.6.0 calls it, and `_get_conn` runs only the
resolution/config column migrations. mani was therefore orphaned under 0.6 --
which is why it has no seeds.jsonl beside its db. The differential's premise
(compare 0.6 behaviour with 0.7's) is vacuous on this store the way it is on
the two empty stores. Making the harness "run to completion" here means giving
it a new mode for "0.6 cannot read this store", which is a decision about what
the safety net proves -- escalated rather than invented.
close_reason: the converter reads a legacy store missing any optional table (relationships, questions, config) as empty and names each absent table; a missing load-bearing seeds table raises a ConversionError naming store and table instead of a bare sqlite3 error. mani's 14 seeds convert and round-trip verify. The 'just differential runs to completion' clause is NOT met and cannot be by this bead - seeds 0.6 cannot read that store either, filed as seeds-4co.27

title: resolve-seeds-from-beads must verify candidates against shipped code, not bead status
description:
The `resolve-seeds-from-beads` skill reports seeds as shipped when they are not. Observed in
a real run 2026-08-31 and recorded in seeds-187's resolution.

## The defect

Step 1 of the skill says to find originating seeds from the beads' "Source:" lineage. No
such field exists in this repo — lineage is PROSE mentions of seed IDs inside bead
descriptions. So recovery is text-matching, and text-matching over-claims: a seed is
reported done when every bead that happens to MENTION it has closed, regardless of whether
any of those beads actually implemented it.

**Concrete false positive:** seeds-lcfa.1.1 (wire seeds sync into git hooks) came back as
shipped. The closed bead that mentioned it (seeds-ww8) had shipped a different, downstream
fix. The seed's actual work was never done.

This is a false positive in the skill responsible for closing the seeds->beads loop, so its
failure mode is silent: it resolves deliberation that no code backs.

## The fix

Change the skill so a candidate is verified against SHIPPED CODE before being offered for
resolution — the file, function or behaviour the seed called for must actually exist. Bead
status is a hint for finding candidates, never evidence that the work happened.

State this explicitly in the skill text, with the seeds-lcfa.1.1 case as the worked example,
so it is not re-simplified back into "the bead closed, therefore it shipped."

## Scope

One file: `src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/skills/resolve-seeds-from-beads/SKILL.md`.
No Python changes.

## Why P1 and why now

It affects the 149 already-closed beads whose lineage is prose-only. The companion bead
(add a structured Source field) only helps beads written from now on and does nothing for
that backlog, so this is the half that fixes what already exists.

## Out of scope

- Adding the Source field (separate bead).
- The backlog-triage gap seeds-187 also names ("the skill assumes one just-finished feature
  and says nothing about 38 stale candidates") — that is now covered by `winnow`
  (seeds-dqu / seeds-84h), not by this skill.

## Acceptance

- The skill requires code-level verification before offering a candidate.
- The seeds-lcfa.1.1 over-claim is documented in the skill as the reason.
- pytest and `seeds check` green.
design: From seeds-187's resolution, written after the first real run. Not a fork with the Source-field bead: 149 closed beads already carry prose-only lineage, so a new field cannot help them -- code verification is what fixes the existing backlog.
acceptance_criteria: resolve-seeds-from-beads/SKILL.md requires each candidate to be verified against shipped code before being offered for resolution, treats bead status as a discovery hint only, and documents the seeds-lcfa.1.1 false positive as the rationale; no Python changes; pytest and seeds check green.

title: Convert splits a multi-line legacy title at its first blank line, and normalizes leading body whitespace
description:
Two rulings from @aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01, both found by the differential harness after the answers-edge fix unblocked two of three repos.

PART 1 - MULTI-LINE LEGACY TITLES. code_set_catalog is the last blocked repo. Past the answers rows it dies on SeedFileError: field title: title must be one non-empty line. Two seeds of 435 carry a title that is really a title PLUS a whole body: csc-94 is 7 lines / 649 chars and csc-180 is 10 lines / 1442 chars. In BOTH, line 1 is a genuine question, line 2 is blank, and the rest is elaboration - someone pasted a multi-paragraph thought into the title field.

RULED: split at the first blank line. Line 1 becomes the title; the remainder is prepended to the body. The split follows the shape the data already has rather than inventing a boundary, and nothing is lost. Convert must NAME each seed it split, the way it names dropped fixtures and dropped answers edges - a silent content move is exactly what this project keeps refusing.

Rejected: refusing the repo, which blocks 435 seeds over 2 records; and relaxing the one-line title rule, which would make seeds list print a 1,442-character title and empty the rule of meaning.

PART 2 - LEADING BODY WHITESPACE. Five code_collector seeds have a 0.6 body starting with a newline, which conversion strips. Verified not content loss: the text is fully intact, e.g. "\\nInventoried the SAS truncated-operator idiom..." becomes "Inventoried the SAS truncated-operator idiom...".

RULED: intended normalization, exactly as the trailing newline already is. So state it in docs/storage-format.md section 2 - a body carries no leading or trailing blank lines - and give the harness a body-leading-newline allowlist entry MATCHED NARROWLY: the two strings equal after stripping leading newlines, never a blanket ignore on body differences. That takes code_collector from 12 regressions to 0.

Source: bead seeds-4co.24, bead seeds-4co.17
acceptance_criteria: A legacy seed whose title spans multiple lines converts: the first line becomes the title, the remainder is prepended to the body with nothing lost, and convert names each seed it split. code_set_catalog (435 seeds, 2 such titles) converts to completion and 'seeds check' is clean on the output. docs/storage-format.md states that a body carries no leading or trailing blank lines. The differential harness gains a body-leading-newline allowlist entry matched narrowly - equal after stripping leading newlines - and code_collector reports 0 regressions.
notes: Split rule implemented in precedence order per the 2026-09-01 ruling: (1) a blank line whose position leaves a ONE-LINE title (i.e. line 2) cuts there; (2) otherwise the first sentence end strictly INSIDE line 1 cuts there; (3) otherwise the end of line 1. Two deliberate picks inside that: (a) rule 1 fires only where it yields a one-line title -- a first blank line further down would leave a still-multi-line title, so the cut is made by rule 2/3 and REPORTED as the rule that actually made it (the moved text is identical either way; only the reported rule differs, and it should be true); (b) a sentence end at the very end of line 1 is reported as 'at first line', not 'at sentence end', so 'at sentence end' means only the genuinely risky mid-line cut. Abbreviation guard: a stop counts only when followed by whitespace then (optional opening punctuation and) a capital, AND the preceding token is neither in a 32-entry abbreviation list (e.g, i.e, vs, cf, Dr, Fig, No, etc...) nor a single letter (which covers e.g./i.e./U.S. structurally). Version strings like v2023.1 are excluded by the whitespace requirement alone. Pinned by tests including a title with 'e.g.' mid-sentence. Both real records (csc-94, csc-180) hit rule 1; rules 2 and 3 fire on no data we have.
close_reason: convert splits a multi-line legacy title (blank line, else first sentence end with an abbreviation guard, else first line) reporting which rule cut each seed; the body's no-leading-or-trailing-blank-lines rule is stated in the spec and allowlisted narrowly in the harness; all seven convertible repos now report 0 regressions

title: seeds convert CRASHES with a bare traceback on a legacy DB carrying an 'answers' relationship (3 of 13 unconverted repos)
description:
Found by the differential harness (seeds-4co.17) on its first real multi-repo run, 2026-09-01.

seeds.legacy.get_relationships builds RelationType(row['rel_type']) eagerly for every relationships row it reads out of the pre-0.7 SQLite. A row whose rel_type is outside the closed set raises a bare ValueError that nothing catches, so 'seeds convert' dies with a Python traceback:

    ValueError: 'answers' is not a valid RelationType

The JSONL side of the same converter already handles this correctly -- convert.py's _halves_from_jsonl catches the ValueError and re-raises ConversionError naming the file, the line, the seed id and the rule ("outside the closed set (relates-to, questions, questioned-by) ... §5.2"). Only the DB path is missing that treatment, so which of the two stores holds the bad row decides whether the operator gets a diagnostic or a stack trace.

MEASURED across ~/projects/outins, 2026-09-01 -- 3 of the 13 unconverted repos carry 'answers' edges in .seeds/seeds.db and therefore cannot be converted at all today:

    code_set_catalog   answers: 3    (questions: 62, relates-to: 2082)
    code_collector     answers: 1    (questions: 5,  relates-to: 286)
    habituate          answers: 1    (questions: 1,  relates-to: 16)

'answers' predates the v2 question-seeds migration; it is the inverse of 'questions' under the old two-object model. Two things need deciding and neither is a code-only call, so this is filed rather than fixed:

  1. Does 'answers' translate (to a 'questions' half in the other direction, most likely) or is it dropped like the legacy questions table, with the row count reported?
  2. Either way the DB path must fail the way the JSONL path does -- a ConversionError naming the seed and the rel_type -- rather than as an unhandled ValueError.

Reproduce:
    just differential ~/projects/outins/code_set_catalog
which reports:
    REFUSED  ...: seeds convert CRASHED on this store, so 0.7 behaviour cannot be observed at all: ValueError: 'answers' is not a valid RelationType
notes:
RULED (@aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01): DROP the legacy answers rows and report the count, exactly as the legacy questions table is handled.

Consistent with the ruling that retired the type: answers was a fossil no workflow ever produced. seeds answer stores an answer as the question-seed content and never made an edge; the only route to one was a hand-run seeds link --type answers. Measured across the unconverted repos: 5 answers rows in total (code_set_catalog 3, code_collector 1, habituate 1) against 2,384 relates-to and 68 questions.

Rejected: translating an answers edge A->B into a reversed questions/questioned-by pair B->A. It would preserve 5 edges by inventing a semantic nobody ever chose, for a relation already ruled vestigial. Also rejected: refusing the conversion, which blocks 3 repos until each is hand-cleaned for 5 rows.

THE OTHER HALF OF THE FIX, and it is the more important one: seeds.legacy.get_relationships builds RelationType(row["rel_type"]) eagerly with nothing catching it, so the operator gets a bare Python traceback. The JSONL side of the SAME converter already does this correctly - a ConversionError naming the file, line, seed id and the closed-set rule. So which of the two source stores holds a bad row currently decides whether you get a diagnostic or a stack trace. Any UNRECOGNISED rel_type must produce that same named diagnostic; only the known-vestigial answers is dropped silently-but-counted.

Reproduce: just differential ~/projects/outins/code_set_catalog

IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-01 (seeds-4co.24/legacy-answers-rows).

DESIGN PICK 1 -- both readers drop, not just the SQLite one. The bead
described the JSONL path as "already correct". It was correct about an
UNRECOGNISED value, but 'answers' is not merely unrecognised: it is the
known-vestigial one the ruling says to drop. Measured on the real repos: the
legacy JSONL is an export OF the legacy SQLite, so it carries the same rows,
and fixing only legacy.py moved all three repos from a bare ValueError to a
ConversionError refusal -- still 0 of 3 convertible, one message later. The
ruling ("drop the answers rows and report the count") and the acceptance
criterion (the harness runs to completion) both require the drop at whichever
reader sees the row. Unrecognised NON-vestigial values still raise
ConversionError from either store, in one shared wording.

DESIGN PICK 2 -- the reported count is distinct EDGES, deduplicated across the
two stores, not raw rows. One dropped edge is normally two rows (SQLite + its
JSONL export); reporting "6" for code_set_catalog's 3 edges would read as data
the converter never had. Counted table-wide rather than while reading, so an
answers edge naming a deleted seed is still counted.

TWO SEPARATE DEFECTS UNCOVERED, both previously hidden behind this crash and
NOT fixed here:
1. code_set_catalog still cannot convert -- for an unrelated reason. Past the
   answers rows it now dies with SeedFileError: field 'title': title must be
   one non-empty line. A legacy seed (a csc question about version labels)
   carries a multi-paragraph blob in its title column. The converter has no
   diagnostic for it and no rule for what a multi-line legacy title becomes.
2. code_collector reports 12 regressions, all one shape: a body whose 0.6
   content began with a leading newline loses it under 0.7 ("\nInventoried..."
   -> "Inventoried..."). Six 'export: content differs' plus their six matching
   'show' findings. Either the leading-newline strip is intended and belongs
   on the harness allowlist beside body-trailing-newline, or it is real body
   loss. Not ruled, so not touched.
close_reason: both legacy readers now drop vestigial 'answers' edges and report the deduplicated count; any other unrecognised rel_type raises a ConversionError naming the store, seed, value and closed set from either path instead of a bare ValueError; habituate and code_collector now convert, code_set_catalog is blocked by a separate unruled defect

title: seeds convert should stage the JSONL for deletion when git holds it, and stop telling people to keep the file
description:
Ruled by @aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01: "if we can delete seeds.jsonl, that should be done as part of the conversion -- probably label it for deletion from the git repo if they are using git".

His caveat is the load-bearing part. TESTED 2026-09-01: in a clone of this repo, deleting the working .seeds/seeds.jsonl and committing the deletion left "seeds history seeds-lcfa" rendering all 9 revisions unchanged. seeds history reads git log / git show against the path, so it needs the HISTORY, not the working file.

THE THREE CONDITIONS, all required, because each failure mode destroys the pre-conversion record outright:
1. the repo is a git work tree
2. .seeds/seeds.jsonl is TRACKED
3. it has no uncommitted changes -- an uncommitted delta exists nowhere else

Fail any one and the file is left alone, with convert naming which. "Label it for deletion" means STAGE the removal (git rm --cached / stage the delete) so it lands in the same commit as the 300-odd new .md files, rather than deleting behind the operator back.

THE COUNTERINTUITIVE PART, worth stating in the output: seeds.jsonl is the SAFE one to delete because git holds it, and seeds.db is the DANGEROUS one because .seeds/.gitignore excludes *.db so git holds nothing. The derived store feels disposable and is the one with no safety net. Convert must not delete seeds.db.

CONSEQUENCE FOR REVERT: today it is "rm -rf .seeds/seeds/" with the old store sitting right there. Once the deletion is staged it becomes "rm -rf .seeds/seeds/" plus restoring the JSONL from the index or from HEAD. Convert must print the exact command for the state it just created rather than the generic one.

DOCS TO CORRECT -- three places say to keep the FILE, which conflates it with its history and is wrong now that this is tested:
- src/seeds/cli.py:1814  "Keep seeds.jsonl in the repository afterwards"
- src/seeds/history.py:21  "must never be filtered out of the repository"
- docs/storage-format.md:488  same wording
The accurate rule is narrower and stronger: the file is disposable; its git history must never be rewritten or filtered.

Source: seeds-4co.14, seeds-sdhc.5
acceptance_criteria: In a git work tree where .seeds/seeds.jsonl is tracked and clean, 'seeds convert' stages its deletion so the removal lands in the same commit as the conversion, prints the exact revert command, and says the pre-conversion history is preserved in git. When the repo is not a git work tree, or the JSONL is untracked, or it has uncommitted changes, the file is LEFT ALONE and convert says which of the three conditions failed. seeds.db is never deleted. The three places claiming the file must be kept are corrected to say the HISTORY must be kept.
notes:
REFRAMED 2026-09-01, and this raises its priority: deleting the JSONL is NOT tidiness, it closes a silent-wrongness hole.

Measured on this repo six hours after conversion: the leftover .seeds/seeds.jsonl holds 314 records while the tree holds 309, and seeds-dv6r -- created after conversion -- is in the tree and absent from the JSONL. The file does not merely stop being written; it starts LYING immediately while still looking authoritative.

Why that matters concretely: transcript evidence shows 35 genuine cross-repo queries across 18 sessions, all shell loops reading .seeds/seeds.jsonl directly with python/awk/grep across many repos. Against a converted repo every one of those keeps working, returns pre-conversion data, and reports no error. Plausible output, silently wrong -- the exact class this storage overhaul existed to kill, reintroduced by leaving the old file in place.

So the deletion is the fix for a live defect, not housekeeping. It also means the three conditions matter more, not less: where the file CANNOT be safely deleted (no git, untracked, or dirty), convert should say plainly that the leftover JSONL is now stale and must not be read.
IMPL 2026-09-01 (branch seeds-4co.18/conversion-messaging). Three deliberate picks, each a 2-way code-only choice:

(1) A FOURTH blocking condition beyond the three in the bead: an unresolved fork also leaves seeds.jsonl alone. A fork is finished by editing the .md and RE-RUNNING the converter (convert._write_tree explicitly supports that path and preserves a hand-resolved body). A re-run reads the UNION of both stores; with the JSONL already gone from the working tree the second run would see only the database and silently overwrite the half the operator was merging. So the second source stays until the merge it is a source for is done. Alternative considered and rejected: stage unconditionally and rely on the printed revert command.

(2) Git process plumbing (GitUnavailable, the text/bytes subprocess runners, repo_root) MOVED from seeds/githistory.py down into seeds/gitstage.py, which is now the single door for git in src/ the way tests/githelpers.py is in tests/. githistory is read-only by design and this bead needed a WRITE (git rm). Alternative rejected: a second, duplicated subprocess wrapper in gitstage — that is exactly the shape test_git_single_door.py exists to prevent on the test side.

(3) 'git rm' rather than 'git rm --cached'. --cached would leave the retired file sitting on disk, which is the entire hazard being removed (a file that looks authoritative while nothing updates it). The removal is STAGED, not committed, so it still lands in the operator's own commit.

Related defect fixed in passing: the revert command never removed .seeds/config.yaml, which convert writes. It is now assembled from what the run actually did, config.yaml included when this run wrote it.

Fifth doc repeating 'never delete the file' found beyond the three named: README.md's 'Converting a pre-0.7 project' section. Corrected with the others.
close_reason: seeds convert stages the retired JSONL for deletion when git holds a clean tracked copy, prints a revert command assembled from what the run actually did, and leaves the file alone naming which of FOUR conditions failed; seeds.db is never deleted; five docs corrected from 'keep the file' to 'never rewrite the history'

title: Conversion is on-demand, so the refusal message IS the migration UX — and three commands skip it
description:
Ruled by @aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01. There is no batch rollout: "we will simply convert them as we go to use seeds in them the first time -- this is how most people are probably going to do a similar conversion".

That is almost certainly right, and it has a consequence the plan never costed: if conversion happens on first contact, then the refusal message and seeds convert output ARE the migration experience. Not a migration guide, not a batch tool. Whatever a stranger sees at that moment is the whole of it.

His stated expectation, which is the acceptance criterion: any attempt to add, read or update seed data warns the database is out of date, says to run seeds convert when ready, and stops.

MEASURED 2026-09-01 against a copy of an unconverted repo. 19 of 22 data-touching commands already do exactly that -- list, ready, show, tree, search, questions, blocked, deferred, recent, jot, create, update, resolve, explore, defer, abandon, link, ask, retype, history, prefix, doctor all exit 1 naming seeds convert. Three do not:

1. **seeds prime exits 0 and emits normal workflow context with no warning at all.** This is the serious one. prime is what an agent reads at session start and is wired into hooks, so on an unconverted repo an agent is handed healthy-looking context and no signal that the store is stale -- the exact silent wrongness this storage change existed to escape, reintroduced at the migration boundary.
2. seeds export --json exits 1 but says "no seed-file store at <path>" instead of naming seeds convert.
3. seeds check exits 1 and reports store-missing as a bare path. Defensible for a diagnostic, but inconsistent with the other 19.

SEPARATE, SMALLER, AND REAL: seeds jot TEXT refuses correctly but does NOT echo the text back, so the thought exists only in terminal scrollback. jot is the minimum-friction capture verb whose entire purpose is catching a thought before it escapes, and the first encounter with an unconverted repo will often happen mid-thought. Refusing is right; losing the text is not.

Source: seeds-4co.14, seeds-tz66
acceptance_criteria: Every command that reads, adds or updates seed data on an unconverted repo warns that the store is out of date and names 'seeds convert', and exits non-zero. 'seeds prime' in particular must not return normal-looking context with exit 0. 'seeds jot TEXT' prints the text back so it is recoverable, plus the exact command to re-run after converting. A test covers prime and jot specifically.
notes:
RULED (@aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01) on seeds prime specifically: it must NOT abort. It produces its normal output and then reports that the store needs converting.

His reasoning is right and the measurement makes it stronger. prime is ~192 lines: a large static instruction block (rules, verbs, capture guidance) followed by a live-state block built from store.list_seeds -- counts, recently-updated, active exploration, open questions, tag clusters. On an unconverted repo the static half renders fine and the state block is SILENTLY ABSENT. No error, no gap marker, exit 0. An agent reading that has no reason to suspect anything is missing and concludes the project has no seeds; pman has 29 sitting in SQLite.

So aborting would be doubly wrong -- the agent loses the verbs AND stays uninformed.

PLACEMENT MATTERS, not just presence. A warning appended at line 192 arrives after the agent has formed its picture. Put the notice WHERE THE STATE BLOCK WOULD HAVE BEEN, so the absence is explained at the point of absence, plus a line near the top since long context is read top-down and sometimes truncated.

DO NOT read the legacy store to report a count (asked and declined): prime stays free of any SQLite import, keeping the legacy reader confined to convert.py where the cutover deliberately put it. Say the state is unavailable, say existing seeds are NOT lost, and name seeds convert.

Exit code stays 0 -- prime produced usable output, and it is consumed as text by an agent via hooks, so the signal belongs in the text rather than in a status a hook would trip over.
close_reason: all 24 data-touching verbs now name seeds convert and exit non-zero, enforced as a parametrized invariant; prime keeps exit 0 and carries the notice twice - a banner before the heading and the full explanation where the state block would have been - and is asserted to import no sqlite; jot echoes the thought shlex-quoted for re-running

title: Differential harness: prove 0.7 storage causes no behavioural degradation, per repo
description:
Ruled by @aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01, as the way to prove the storage change costs nothing behaviourally before it ships: "we probably want to think of ways of comparing/checking on seeds behavior under the new storage to ensure no degradation."

THE SHAPE: for one repo, take its pre-conversion store. Run a fixed command set under 0.6 against SQLite, capture the outputs. Convert a copy. Run the same command set under 0.7 against the tree. Diff. Anything not on a declared allowlist is a regression.

Commands to cover at minimum: list, list --all, ready, deferred, recent, show, show --full, tree, search, questions, blocked, prime, export.

KNOWN-EXPECTED DIFFERENCES, which is what the allowlist is for. Each needs a written justification, because an allowlist without reasons degrades into "ignore the failures":
- The six ruled test fixtures are dropped, so any repo carrying them has a smaller corpus (this one went 314 -> 308).
- Relationships gain the questioned-by inverse halves, so relationship counts rise (57 edges here).
- Bodies gain a canonical trailing newline (282 of 314 records here differed by nothing else).
- Ranked search is gone: seeds suggest no longer exists, and seeds search is ripgrep, so result ORDER changes (now id-sorted) and Porter stemming is gone ("merging" no longer finds "merge"). This is the accepted casualty, not a regression.
- A resolution/converted_at field appears where the old store had none.

WHY IT IS WORTH BUILDING RATHER THAN EYEBALLING: the conversion has already been observed to be correct on this repo, but this repo is the one the format was designed against. The other 14 stores were written by the same tool over a year and will contain shapes nobody remembers — the vocabulary_formats store already turned up "db-only: 2", two seeds that lived only in SQLite and had never been exported. That case resolved correctly, and it was found by running the converter, not by predicting it.

Source: seeds-sdhc.1, seeds-4co.7, seeds-4co.14
acceptance_criteria: For a given repo, the harness runs the same command set against 0.6+SQLite and against 0.7+converted tree, diffs the outputs, and reports every difference not on a declared allowlist as a regression. Running it on a repo with a known-good conversion produces zero unexplained diffs. Each allowlist entry carries a written justification. Works on a repo the operator has not converted yet, by converting a COPY.
notes:
ADD TO THE HARNESS SCOPE: the 35 cross-repo shell loops found in transcripts (18 sessions) all read .seeds/seeds.jsonl directly. They are a real consumer of the old format and they break -- or worse, silently return stale data -- on a converted repo. The harness should cover the cross-repo case explicitly, not just single-repo command output: run the old glob-the-JSONL recipe and the new "seeds export --json | duckdb" recipe over the same set of repos and diff. That is what proves the replacement is equivalent for the one workflow that spans repos.
DESIGN PICKS (code-only 2-way choices, ruled by me and recorded per the ambiguity rule):

1. The 0.6 side is provisioned with 'git archive v0.6.0 | tar -x' into the run's temp dir, NOT 'git worktree add --detach'. A worktree registers itself inside the shared .git of a repo this harness is only ever allowed to READ, and an interrupted run leaves that registration behind for somebody to find later; an archive touches nothing. --legacy-checkout overrides it with an existing pre-0.7 checkout. (Verified: 'uv run --project <extracted>' builds and reports 'seeds, version 0.6.0'.)

2. The conversion step calls seeds.convert.convert() as a LIBRARY; every command being compared still goes through the CLI as a subprocess. The library call hands back dropped_fixtures, forks and check findings as structure, where the CLI hands back a paragraph -- and parsing that paragraph would be a second place the report format has to stay in step. The distinction held is that the conversion is SETUP, not something under comparison.
close_reason: scripts/differential_harness.py runs the same command set under 0.6+SQLite and 0.7+tree and diffs, with a 12-entry allowlist each carrying a written justification; ran clean on 4 real repos (130 seeds, 0 unexplained diffs), refuses on an empty corpus rather than reporting health, and three injected-fault self-tests prove it can fail

title: Dogfood: convert this repo and use the new format before any public release
description:
Convert this repo and run on the new format in anger, before any public release.

## Why this is a bead and not a checkbox

@aguynamedryan, on the release plan: 0.7 is the storage format change, and he **dogfoods the conversion and sustained use on his own seeds before any public release**. seeds-02ur — 36 orphaned rows still sitting here from the v2 question-seeds migration — is standing evidence that migrations in this repo leave debris that nobody notices for months.

## What this covers

- Run the converter on the real `.seeds/` (306+ seeds, 549 relationships, 75 of 304 ids dotted).
- Confirm round-trip verification passes and a second run is byte-idempotent.
- **Leave the old store in place.** Do not delete `.seeds/seeds.db` or `.seeds/seeds.jsonl` — reverting must stay `rm -rf .seeds/seeds/` until @aguynamedryan rules otherwise.
- Use it for real deliberation for a stretch, then report what broke.
- Only after that: decide on public release, and on retiring the old store.

Source: seeds-sdhc, seeds-sdhc.1, seeds-02ur
acceptance_criteria: The converter has run on this repo's real .seeds/, round-trip verification passed, a second run was byte-idempotent, .seeds/seeds.db and .seeds/seeds.jsonl are still present, and sustained real use has been reported back to @aguynamedryan.
close_reason: Converted this repo: 314 source records -> 308 seed files, all db-extends-disk, no forks; round-trip verified, seeds check clean, second run byte-identical; seeds.db and seeds.jsonl left in place so revert is rm -rf .seeds/seeds/. Commands verified against the real tree incl. seeds history reading across the conversion boundary. NOT done and not mine to do: the sustained-real-use half of the acceptance - @aguynamedryan reports that back himself

title: seeds export --json: a stdout pipe replacing the tracked JSONL
description:
Add `seeds export --json`: emit the whole corpus as JSON to **stdout**. A pipe, not a tracked file.

## This ships in 0.7, not later

Killing the tracked JSONL costs **availability, not speed**, and that distinction is why this cannot be deferred. Today `grep .seeds/seeds.jsonl` and DuckDB-over-JSONL both work with seeds not installed and no parser written by the caller. The 35 ms frontmatter-scan measurement answers the wrong objection — it proves reading markdown is fast, not that anything else can read it.

**13 repos of cross-project query (seeds-183) break on conversion day** if this is not there. Concretely, the existing recipe globs `.seeds/seeds.jsonl` across `~/projects/outins/*/` (1,161 seeds, 57 ms) and it stops working the moment the file stops being written.

## Shape

Nothing tracked, nothing to diverge, nothing to destroy. If ad-hoc SQL is wanted, the caller pipes this into DuckDB on demand.

Source: seeds-sdhc, seeds-183, seeds-lcfa.6
acceptance_criteria: 'seeds export --json' writes the whole corpus as JSON to stdout and creates no file; piping it into DuckDB answers the cross-project query that today globs .seeds/seeds.jsonl.
notes:
DESIGN PICKS (code-only 2-way choices, ruled per the overnight ambiguity rule):

1. OUTPUT SHAPE: JSONL — one JSON object per newline-terminated line — NOT a single JSON array. DuckDB read_json_auto reads either, so the array buys nothing, while JSONL keeps two things the array loses: a grep hit is still a whole record (the availability property this bead exists to preserve), and several repos concatenate into one valid stream, which is how the cross-project fan-out is written.

2. MODULE: new src/seeds/jsonexport.py, NOT an addition to export.py. export.py imports db.py at module level; the cutover (seeds-4co.9) deletes db.py, and this must not be entangled with it. jsonexport.py imports only seedfile — the single door — and reads nothing else.

3. BARE `seeds export` REFUSES (exit 2, empty stdout) rather than defaulting to --json. The retired command of that name wrote a tracked file; someone typing it from muscle memory should be told the shape changed, not handed a megabyte on stdout. --json is currently the only format.

4. ALL-OR-NOTHING, not streaming. The whole store is read and validated before the first byte is written, so an unreadable file aborts with empty stdout. A stream that stops after 200 of 308 records is indistinguishable downstream from a repo that has 200 seeds — a short answer to a query that looks exactly like a true one.

5. FIELD NAMES carry over from the retired JSONL (`content`, `seed_type`, and the relationships mapping keys) so queries written against that file keep running. `parent` and `converted_at` are added because the seed files carry them. `format_version` is NOT emitted (storage-format §8: the frozen format has no version, and a discriminator on a derived stream would be a promise to keep versioning something with no versions). Empty optionals are emitted as null/""/[] rather than omitted, so a column's existence does not depend on which seeds a repo happens to have.

VERIFIED against a converted copy of this repo's own corpus in a temp dir (308 seeds): the exported `content` is byte-identical to the .md body for 308/308; vs the retired JSONL the only deltas are the converter's own (old content is a prefix of new for 308/308 — db-extends-disk; new relationships are a superset of old for 308/308 — edges now stored at both ends, §5.1). Export with seeds.db and seeds.jsonl deleted still emits all 308, proving it reads only .seeds/seeds/.
close_reason: src/seeds/jsonexport.py + 'seeds export --json' emits one JSON object per line to stdout, creating no file; reads the new store only through seedfile; verified end-to-end by piping into duckdb read_json_auto including the seeds-183 cross-project query across two repos

title: Point every command at the tree and delete the SQLite persistence layer
description:
Point every CLI verb at the markdown tree through the reader/writer module, and delete the SQLite persistence layer.

## Scope

- Every command reads and writes seed files. No command touches SQLite.
- `src/seeds/db.py` goes, along with the `.seeds/seeds.db` lifecycle, the FTS5 tables, and `seeds sync` / `seeds import` / the divergence machinery in `export.py` (`find_divergence`, `db_extends_disk`, `FUTURE_TIMESTAMP_TOLERANCE`), which exist only to police a two-store world that no longer exists.
- `seeds doctor` loses its sync checks. What replaces them is `seeds check` — see the sibling beads; do not leave doctor reporting green on checks that no longer mean anything.

## Locked decision: "drop SQLite" does NOT mean "swap in DuckDB"

It means delete the persistence layer. Measured (seeds-lcfa.6, titan 2026-08-25): 280 seeds — pure Python 47 ms, DuckDB 60 ms; 5,040 seeds — pure Python 297 ms, DuckDB 427 ms. Python wins at both scales because the work is file I/O, not query planning, and `seeds show <id>` degenerates to a single file read. DuckDB's genuine place is cross-project reading, over the `seeds export --json` pipe.

## Hazards this deletes, worth knowing so they are not reintroduced

- the content-divergence deadlock (a body edit becomes an ordinary file edit; there is no wholesale rewrite to guard)
- timestamps as authority, and with them `FUTURE_TIMESTAMP_TOLERANCE`
- the wholesale-rewrite destruction surface

Source: seeds-sdhc, seeds-fkb8, seeds-lcfa.6, seeds-ebg1
acceptance_criteria: No command imports db.py; src/seeds/db.py and the .seeds/seeds.db lifecycle are removed along with sync, import, find_divergence, db_extends_disk and FUTURE_TIMESTAMP_TOLERANCE; 'seeds doctor' no longer reports two-store sync checks; the full test suite passes.
notes:
RULING (@aguynamedryan, 2026-08-31) on a gap seeds-4co.1 surfaced: the project prefix currently lives in the SQLite config table this bead deletes (db.get_prefix, db.py:316). It moves to a small tracked .seeds/config.yaml holding 'prefix:'. Not a frontmatter field (312 copies of one value), and not derived from filenames (an empty repo has no prefix to read, so seeds init would have nothing to record). Specified in docs/storage-format.md section 9.
ACCEPTANCE-CRITERIA GAP (recorded 2026-08-31): the acceptance criteria do not mention the project prefix moving to .seeds/config.yaml, though the ruling is in the notes above. NOTE it is now PARTLY DONE: seeds-4co.6's converter already writes .seeds/config.yaml with the prefix, because conversion is the last moment the SQLite config table can be read. This bead must confirm every command reads the prefix from there once db.py is deleted.
Design picks recorded during implementation (2-way, code-only, per the overnight ruling):
1. A new src/seeds/store.py holds the set operations over the tree rather than inlining them in cli.py -- prime.py needs the same reads, and cli.py was already 2457 lines. seedfile.py stays the ONLY parser/writer; store.py never touches bytes.
2. Commands operate on seedfile.SeedRecord directly, NOT on models.Seed. Round-tripping through Seed would silently drop 'parent' and 'converted_at' on every write, which is data loss the type system would not catch.
3. models.Seed and models.Relationship stay in models.py (docstringed as legacy, conversion-path only) rather than moving into seeds.legacy -- less churn, and models.py is the natural home for a record shape.
4. Store.rename_prefix writes with touch=False. A rename is not deliberation, and bumping updated_at across the whole corpus would erase the 'updated_at == created_at means never edited' test (storage-format.md §3) for every seed at once. The SQLite version did not touch it either.
5. seeds init no longer writes .seeds/.gitignore. Its only content was *.db patterns; with no database it would be vestigial. Existing .gitignores are left alone -- they ignore nothing the tree needs.
6. seeds retype drops its sidecar .db backup instead of gaining a tree equivalent. The files are tracked; git diff/checkout is the better backup.
7. prime.py's SESSION CLOSE PROTOCOL now says 'seeds check' where it said 'seeds sync --flush-only'. There is nothing to flush; check is the honest analogue and a shipped verb.
8. staged_paths_outside removed from gitstage.py (dead once sync went -- its premise was a pending export a commit could capture). _subprocess_env kept: it describes git's hook contract, and githistory.py + tests/githelpers.py both need it.
close_reason: db.py and export.py deleted; every command reads/writes the tree through seedfile via the new store.py; sync and import removed; doctor's two-store checks gone; a read-only LegacyDatabase in legacy.py (opened mode=ro) survives on the conversion path only, since convert must still read unconverted repos

title: Converter: round-trip verification and byte-idempotence
description:
Make the converter prove its own output before anyone trusts it.

## Round-trip verification, inside the converter

Re-read the emitted markdown tree, rebuild the record set, and diff it field-by-field against the union input. Fail on any difference outside an explicit normalization allowlist (whitespace, key ordering). Then run `seeds check` on the output before the source store is left alone.

**Why this is a requirement and not polish:** the data-pipeline standard's rule — the code deciding "clean" is itself code that can be silently wrong. A converter that reports success is a stale-check, and an untested one lies.

There is a worked dry run to model it on: commit 1afc51c (the seeds-wurl title repair) verified 306 records in and out, id set unchanged, 83 titles restored, 0 path-shaped titles remaining, and no field other than title and its updated_at differing on any record.

## Byte-idempotence

A second run against an unchanged store must leave `git diff` empty. This is a stronger property than "non-destructive" and much cheaper to assert in a test.

## Fixtures

- This repo's real `.seeds/` (306+ seeds, 549 relationships).
- A synthetic repo built to exhibit **all four divergence cases at once**, so the classifier is exercised rather than assumed.

Source: seeds-sdhc.1, seeds-wurl
acceptance_criteria: The converter re-reads its own output, rebuilds the record set, diffs field-by-field against the union input, fails on any difference outside a declared normalization allowlist, and runs 'seeds check' on the output before finishing; a second run on an unchanged store leaves 'git diff' empty; fixtures include this repo and a synthetic repo exhibiting all four divergence cases.
notes:
Design picks made while building the verification half (2026-08-31):

1. Verification is TWO passes, not one. The round-trip pass diffs the re-read
   tree against the union record (catches a writer and reader that disagree).
   A second pass diffs it against the RAW STORES (catches a union step that
   was itself wrong) -- a converter verified only against its own intermediate
   agrees with itself. tests/test_convert.py::TestVerificationCatchesLies
   hands it four specific lies, one of which only the source pass can see.

2. seeds check runs on the output, but the conflict-markers finding on a file
   THIS RUN wrote as a fork is filtered out of the gate: it says the same
   thing the fork report already says and would bury findings that are not
   expected. Every other finding on that same file is still reported. Forks
   keep ConversionReport.clean False, so the exit status stays non-zero until
   a human resolves them.

3. A fork file found ALREADY RESOLVED by hand is left alone on a re-run and
   reported. Re-emitting the conflict would destroy a resolution that lives
   only in the tree -- the one way a re-run could lose deliberation. Its body
   is then excluded from the source-containment assertion, because it is
   deliberately neither source body.

Measured: real corpus (314 records copied to a temp dir) -> 308 files, check
clean, second run leaves git diff empty. Synthetic four-case store exercises
all four classes at once.
Correctness fix after coordinator review (2026-08-31), and it was a real gap:

'seeds check' EXITS 0 ON AN EMPTY STORE -- verified here: an emptied
.seeds/seeds/ returns [] findings, exit 0. So 'the converter ran check on its
output and it passed' was not evidence the conversion produced anything. My
first cut had verify() demand a file for every id IN THE UNION, but nothing
asserted the union covered the sources -- a short or empty union sailed
through and check agreed.

verify() now runs a COMPLETENESS pass first (convert._assert_complete), on
SETS rather than counts because equal counts still hide a swap:

  1. the union's id set == source ids minus the declared drops, naming both
     directions of the difference;
  2. an explicit zero-file guard, worded at the failure it exists for;
  3. every expected id has a file, naming the missing ids (capped at 20, then
     counted);
  4. source_ids - present - drop_ids is empty -- the declared drops are the
     ONLY permitted absences, and an undeclared one is a hard error, never a
     warning.

drop_ids is threaded from convert() into verify(). The report now prints the
arithmetic ('314 seed(s) in the source stores -> 308 converted') so the count
is checkable by eye.

Six tests in TestCompletenessOutranksCheck, each asserting BOTH halves -- that
check is green on the broken tree AND that verification refuses it -- because
the first half is what makes the second necessary.

Confirmed the coordinator's number independently: converted output reports 0
check findings, down from the 57 one-sided 'questions' edges a corpus rendered
without the questioned-by inverses produces. Not partial: exactly 0.
FOLLOW-UP after the first close (commit b2798fc, merged a43eb1e). The first cut of verify() demanded a file for every id IN THE UNION but never asserted the union covered the sources, so a short or empty conversion passed with 'seeds check' nodding along. Measured on the merged checker: an empty .seeds/seeds/ reports '0 files, no violations' and exits 0, while the same corpus rendered in full reports 57 violations and exits 1. verify() now runs _assert_complete FIRST, on sets rather than counts: union id set == source ids minus declared drops, an explicit zero-file guard, every expected id has a file (naming the missing ones), and declared drops are the ONLY permitted absences. Six tests in TestCompletenessOutranksCheck each assert BOTH that check is green on a deliberately broken tree AND that verification refuses it. The report now prints '314 seed(s) in the source stores -> 308 converted'.
close_reason: convert() verifies before returning: a round-trip pass and a second pass against the raw stores, six declared normalizations each with a written justification, then seeds check on the output; byte-idempotent second run asserted in tests; TestVerificationCatchesLies proves verify() rejects four specific lies

title: Converter: union input, four-way divergence classification, forks as conflict files
description:
Build the converter that turns an existing seeds repo — including one whose DB and JSONL have diverged — into the markdown tree.

@aguynamedryan set the bar in one sentence, 2026-08-31: **"just fucking make sure that we get the data in correctly."**

## The input is the UNION, never one side

Convert from `DB ∪ JSONL`, per id and per field. Never "convert the DB, then reconcile the JSONL against it" — that rebuilds the derived-store-overwrites-durable-store shape (seeds-fkb8) inside the migration itself.

## Divergence is four conditions; only three may be auto-resolved

Classify every id before writing anything:

1. **DB only** — never exported. seeds-fkb8 itself was in this state on 2026-08-28.
2. **JSONL only** — the import aborted above it or skipped it. @markdanese's 40 seeds (seeds-1x6b).
3. **Both, DB content extends disk content** — the ordinary append; the DB wins. `db_extends_disk`'s docstring records 41 of 42 content edits across 67 commits were literal appends, so this is the common case.
4. **Both, neither prefixes the other** — a genuine fork.

**Case 4 must NEVER be auto-resolved.** Picking a winner there is precisely the silent-collapse error the deliberation caught itself making twice — once for `merge=union` plus timestamp collapse, and once already recorded about cr-sqlite in seeds-lcfa.4.

## A fork converts to a file, not an error

Emit `<id>.md` carrying both bodies with git conflict markers, so it is resolved with ordinary merge tooling. Today the same situation is a deadlock the operator clears by hand-rebuilding a body and handing it back. The new architecture is good at exactly one thing the old one was not: representing a conflict as text a human can read.

## Git history is a third input, not just provenance

seeds-wurl proves both live stores can agree and both be wrong — 83 titles corrupt in DB and JSONL simultaneously, with git holding the only correct copy. Mine the ~113 commits touching `.seeds/seeds.jsonl` as the **repair oracle**. Measured 2026-08-31: materialising the JSONL at each commit and pulling one record by id walks all 113 commits in 1.3 s.

## Also drop, do not translate

The legacy `questions` table. Re-measured 2026-08-31: **all 36 of 36 rows are orphaned**, so it is entirely debris from the v2 question-seeds migration (seeds-02ur).

## Non-destructive

Write the tree alongside the existing store. **Never delete the source until @aguynamedryan says so** — `.seeds/` in this repo is the real design database. Reverting must be `rm -rf .seeds/seeds/`.

## It is a shipped, tested verb

Not a `scripts/` one-shot. 13 repos on titan carry a `.seeds/`, and @markdanese converts on a schedule and version we do not choose. seeds-02ur is standing evidence of what a one-shot leaves behind.

Source: seeds-sdhc.1, seeds-wurl, seeds-fkb8, seeds-1x6b, seeds-02ur, seeds-lcfa.4

title: seeds check: the violations tier (content plausibility, not format validity)
description:
Build `seeds check` — the violations tier. This is the load-bearing detection work, and it must exist before the converter, which calls it against its own output.

## Why this is not a nice-to-have

**Under files-as-truth, today's `doctor` becomes vacuous.** Nearly all of it checks the *relationship between two stores* — JSONL readable, JSONL and DB agree, `find_divergence` clean. There will be no second store, so those checks disappear. If nothing replaces them, 0.7 ships with strictly less detection than 0.6 has.

**What replaces them is a different job: content plausibility, not format validity.** The proof is seeds-wurl — on 2026-08-31 an agent's bulk sweep replaced the title of 83 of 306 seeds with a scratchpad path. Every record parsed perfectly; a path is valid free text. Both stores agreed, so every divergence check was correctly green, and it went unnoticed for three days and three commits.

@aguynamedryan, ruling on the direction: *"Detection, yes. replaced with content plausibility."*

## Violations to implement (exit non-zero, block the commit)

- frontmatter that will not parse
- a `status` outside the closed set
- a title that is a filesystem path, a URL, or empty
- an empty body
- git conflict markers left in a file
- `updated_at` before `created_at`; a timestamp in the future
- a `parent` that disagrees with the dotted id, names a missing file, or forms a cycle
- a relationship naming a file that does not exist
- a one-sided edge (A relates to B, B does not relate back)
- a `[!SUPERSEDED]` marker with no reason clause

Each finding names the file and prints a remediation.

## Locked decision: `status` stays a closed vocabulary

Do NOT open it the way `seed_type` was opened. The asymmetry is deliberate: `seed_type` could open because only `question` carries behaviour, while `status` values drive `list`, `ready`, `blocked`, and every lifecycle transition. An arbitrary status would break lifecycle logic **silently**, which is worse than the crash it replaces. This proposal has been made twice and rejected twice (seeds-ebg1) — do not make it a third time.

## Test it like a detector, not like a feature

The data-pipeline standard applies directly: the code deciding "clean" is itself code that can be silently wrong, and this one gates the conversion. Test on hand-built bad files with hand-computed expected findings, and make it score the whole corpus rather than a sample.

Source: seeds-sdhc.2, seeds-wurl, seeds-ebg1, seeds-02ur
acceptance_criteria: 'seeds check' exits non-zero and names the file for each of: unparseable frontmatter, status outside the closed set, title that is a path/URL/empty, empty body, git conflict markers, updated_at before created_at, future timestamp, parent disagreeing with the dotted id or missing or cyclic, relationship naming a missing file, one-sided edge, [!SUPERSEDED] with no reason clause. Tests use hand-built bad files with hand-computed expected findings.

Evidence: seeds jot creates a title-only seed by design (cli.py:507 builds Seed(id=..., title=thought) with no content), and 31 of 312 seeds have no body, 23 of them question-type where the title IS the question. As a violation this check would fail on 10% of the corpus on day one and on the output of the primary capture verb. It moves to seeds-4co.4.

- 1 record is REFUSED by the strict reader: seeds-sdhc.1 carries a [!SUPERSEDED] marker at the END of a section (body line 22, under "## A fork converts to a file, not to an error"), retiring a paragraph rather than sitting immediately under the heading. §6.1 is explicit that this is a violation and that there is no floating supersession, so the reader raises rather than guessing at the scope. The marker has to be MOVED under the heading it retires (or the retired claim restructured) before that seed converts. Whoever runs the converter (seeds-4co.6) will hit this on the real corpus; `seeds check` (seeds-4co.3) should surface it as a violation with that remediation.

Reproduce: claude_stuff/seedfile-corpus-roundtrip-*.log in the branch worktree records the run.
Design picks made while building the violations tier:

1. NON-CANONICAL BYTES ARE NOT A VIOLATION. §2 fixes the exact byte layout and
   render_seed_file can produce it for comparison, but the reader deliberately
   normalizes leading/trailing blank lines and §2 itself calls canonicality "a
   check question, not a parse question" without naming a tier. 282 of 314
   records differ from canonical form by a trailing newline alone, so as a
   violation it is the empty-body mistake again. Left to the smells tier
   (seeds-4co.4).

2. `=======` is flagged as a conflict marker ONLY in a file that also carries a
   `<<<<<<<` / `|||||||` / `>>>>>>>` line. On its own it is a setext H1
   underline in ordinary markdown; flagging it would be a false positive in a
   body that never conflicted. diff3's `|||||||` is matched too.

   spend its credibility on false positives.

   than a raised error, so every caller has one exit path.

   the consequent parse error — the parse failure is a consequence, and naming
   both doubles the noise on one fix.

6. seedfile.SeedFileError gained a `code` attribute (default "parse-error"),
   set explicitly at the eight raise sites the spec names — status-unknown,

title: Reader/writer module: strict parse, atomic temp-plus-rename write
description:
Build the single module every command goes through to read and write seed files. No command touches a seed file directly.

## Requirements

- **Strict parse.** An invalid field value raises, naming the file, the field, and the value. Do not go lenient — that is the silent wrongness this whole change exists to escape, and it is the settled answer to what was seeds-sdhc open item #1.
- **Atomic write.** Write to a temp file in the same directory, then `os.replace()` into position (atomic on POSIX). This is all that survives of the Maildir detour — @aguynamedryan: *"Maildir is actually trying to solve a series of problems that I'm not concerned about."* Keep the technique, not the framework.
- **Parse the supersede marker** per the spec's scope rule, so callers can ask for live-only or full content.
- **Path from id**, and id from path, as the only place that mapping lives.

## Why strict is safe here

Strictness is only survivable because `seeds check` (sibling bead) names every bad file in one pass, so a strict read failing on the first bad file is not the operator's only feedback channel. Build them as a pair.

From seeds-4co.1: the both-ends relationship rule needs named inverses for the DIRECTIONAL relation types, which have none today. docs/storage-format.md freezes questions -> questioned-by and answers -> answered-by, so this bead must add both members to RelationType. Keep 'answers' and give it an inverse even though the corpus has ZERO answers edges (534 relates-to, 57 questions, 0 answers), so the rule 'every directional type has a named inverse' holds with no exceptions. Do not 'clean up' answers as unused; that was considered and declined.

What changed: the earlier note said only that 'answers' has zero edges. Tracing every reference showed the stronger fact — the answering workflow does not use edges AT ALL and never did. 'seeds answer' (cli.py:1269) stores the answer as the question-seed's own content and re-stamps resolved_at. RelationType.ANSWERS appears only in the enum (models.py:56), a docstring (db.py:610), and the 'seeds link --type' choice list. An edge-based answering model was superseded by the content-field approach before anyone used it.

SO: the closed set is THREE strings — relates-to<->relates-to (534 edges), questions<->questioned-by (57 edges). This bead adds 'questioned-by' to RelationType and REMOVES RelationType.ANSWERS plus the 'answers' choice on 'seeds link --type'. 'seeds answer' is untouched — it never depended on the edge. See docs/storage-format.md, relationship section.

1. The YAML subset is parsed and emitted BY HAND; no pyyaml dependency was added. The format is a closed subset (fixed key set, fixed order, block sequences only, no flow style, no anchors, no multi-doc), and a general parser would have to be un-taught most of it — it accepts the flow form §4 calls a read error and cannot be made to emit the exact byte layout the converter idempotence requirement depends on. Also keeps runtime deps at click alone. Double-quoted scalars are emitted via json.dumps(ensure_ascii=False) and read via json.loads, which is exactly the YAML 1.2 double-quoted form.

2. A new SeedRecord dataclass rather than reusing models.Seed. Cutover (seeds-4co.9) will need a Seed<->SeedRecord bridge; it is deliberately NOT built here.

title: Freeze the on-disk storage format in docs/storage-format.md
description:
Write `docs/storage-format.md`, freezing the on-disk format. Nothing else in this epic starts until it exists, because the reader/writer, the checker, and the converter are each an independent implementation of it and they must not drift.

## What the document must specify

- **Path rule.** `.seeds/seeds/<id>.md`, the filename being the id verbatim, dots included (`seeds-lcfa.6.1.md`). This is load-bearing: `seeds show <id>` computes its path and is a single file read.
- **Every frontmatter field**, with its type and whether it is required. At minimum: id, title, status, type, created_at, updated_at, tags, parent, relationships, resolution, resolved_at.
- **Block sequences for every multi-value field.** @aguynamedryan, ruled 2026-08-28: *"inline doesn't read better to my eyes -- blocks for frontmatter"*. It is also the better merge behaviour — one value per line means two hosts adding different tags touch different lines and merge cleanly, where the inline form collides.
- **The supersede marker grammar and its scope rule** (see seeds-sdhc.3):

      ## Dolt would give us cell-level merge
      > [!SUPERSEDED] 2026-08-28 — ordinary git line-merge surfaces same-field
      > collisions too, so the 120 MB dependency bought nothing.

  Scope is from the marker to the next heading of the same or higher level. That is the entire parse rule. The reason clause after the date is **mandatory**.
- **Relationship representation**, stored at BOTH ends, with the constraint that only symmetric edge types may be; a directional type needs a named inverse at the far end.
- **`parent:` as an explicit field** even though the id is dotted.
- **`converted_at`**, stamped by the converter so `seeds history` knows where to switch sources.

## Locked decisions to state in the document, with their rationale

These are settled. State them so a later reader does not reopen them:

- **Reads are strict.** Files-as-truth makes every command a parser, so a lenient read reintroduces the silent wrongness this change exists to escape.
- **Corrections replace in place; reasoning accumulates.** A fact that turned out false is fixed, prior value in git. A position moved past is marked, never deleted — it is what stops the question being re-litigated.
- **Nothing is destroyed; the RENDER is what is selective.** `seeds show` renders live content by default, `--full` renders everything.
- **Writes are atomic:** temp file plus `os.replace()`.

Source: seeds-sdhc, seeds-sdhc.3, seeds-sdhc.4, seeds-sdhc.5
acceptance_criteria: docs/storage-format.md exists and specifies: the <id>.md path rule, every frontmatter field with type and required-ness, block sequences for multi-value fields, the [!SUPERSEDED] marker grammar and its scope rule, relationships at both ends with the symmetric-only constraint, the explicit parent field, and converted_at.
notes:
Design picks made while writing docs/storage-format.md (each a 2-way call the bead did not pin):

1. Frontmatter key is `type`, not `seed_type`. The bead enumerated "type"; models.py and the JSONL both say `seed_type`. Documented the mapping explicitly so the reader/writer owns the translation and nothing else guesses.
2. Named inverses for the directional relation types. The both-ends + symmetric-only rule requires a named inverse at the far end, and RelationType today has `questions` and `answers` with NO inverses (they are two unrelated directional relations, not a pair). Froze `questions` -> `questioned-by` and `answers` -> `answered-by`, closed set of five stored rel_type values, and noted phase 2 must add the two new members to RelationType. 57 `questions` edges exist in the corpus, so this is not hypothetical.
3. Optional fields are OMITTED when empty (never `tags: []` / `resolution: ""`), and keys are emitted in a fixed order. Both exist to make rewriting an unchanged seed a byte-level no-op, which the converter needs for re-runnable == byte-idempotent.
4. A naive (offset-less) timestamp is a READ ERROR. The JSONL importer treats naive as UTC; that leniency deliberately does not carry over, because strict reads. Converter normalizes once on the way in.
5. `seeds show` default render keeps the retired heading AND its marker line, eliding only the text inside the scope, so a reader sees that something was retired and why. `--full` prints everything.
6. The body must not repeat the title as a heading — title lives in frontmatter only, or `show` prints it twice.
7. NO `format_version` field, and the omission is stated in the doc so it does not get added later.

Also recorded, not decided: the format permits an empty body, but plan phase 3 lists an empty body as a check VIOLATION, and 31 of 312 seeds in this repo currently have one. Converter and checker have to rule on those together. And the project prefix (today in the SQLite `config` table, which phase 5 deletes) has no home yet — flagged in the doc as not settled, since it is not a frontmatter field.

title: Storage overhaul: one markdown file per seed replaces SQLite + the tracked JSONL
description:
Replace the current two-store architecture (SQLite `.seeds/seeds.db` as the working store, a single tracked `.seeds/seeds.jsonl` as the durable one) with one markdown file per seed: `.seeds/seeds/<id>.md`, YAML frontmatter plus body, as the only store.

## Why

The defect, stated precisely in seeds-fkb8: **the derived store is authorized to overwrite the durable one wholesale, and no cheap check tells you when it has gone stale.** Every export is a full-file rewrite from the DB, so any condition leaving the DB stale turns the next *successful* export into a deletion event. seeds survived its one real incident (seeds-1x6b, @markdanese, five weeks of deliberation) by crashing rather than by design.

After: nothing is derived, nothing is authorized to overwrite anything, and a same-seed collision on two hosts is an ordinary git conflict a human can read.

## The plan is written

**`plans/storage-overhaul.md` is the specification.** Read it before starting any child bead. It carries the phase ordering, what is deliberately NOT being done, and the reasoning behind each call. Do not re-derive decisions from the seeds; the plan is the distillation.

## Release shape

0.7. @aguynamedryan dogfoods the conversion and sustained use on this repo before any public release.

title: Nothing runs 'uv lock --check' — a stale uv.lock ships green through CI and the pre-push gate
description:
uv.lock can drift from pyproject.toml and no automated check notices.

Demonstrated, not hypothetical: e789ac8 (Dependabot PR #30) raised the mypy floor to >=2.3.1 in pyproject.toml without regenerating the lock. 'uv lock --check' exits 1 at that commit. It shipped to main, and it is the revision currently installed on titan's nix profile.
