- Back-link = resolution text + a `lodestone` tag. NO schema change. Do NOT add a new field/status/type to the Seed model. A tag keeps promoted seeds queryable by the audit family without a migration, consistent with 147.3's "not a new type/status/field."
- Two-way provenance is a HARD requirement: file->seed (citation in the bullet) AND seed->file (resolution text names the file + date).
- NON-GOAL: the verb does not surface lodestones anywhere (no `seeds lodestones` view, no `prime` injection). The runtime injecting CLAUDE.md/README is the surfacing mechanism. Do not build surfacing.

## Interface
    seeds promote <id> --to <file> --as "<one-line principle>" [--no-resolve] [--section "## Lodestones"]

## Behavior (all deterministic)
1. Load the seed; error cleanly (non-zero exit) if not found — reuse `get_seed_or_exit` in src/seeds/cli.py.
2. Forward-provenance into `<file>`: find-or-create a managed section (heading from `--section`, default `## Lodestones`) and append a bullet of exactly this shape:
       - <principle> — <id>, promoted <YYYY-MM-DD>
   Create the file if it does not exist. If the section heading already exists in the file, append the bullet under it without duplicating the heading. RECOMMENDED: factor the section find-or-create + append as a PURE string function (text_in -> text_out, e.g. in src/seeds/export.py or a small helper module) so it is unit-testable without touching the filesystem.
3. Back-provenance onto the seed: set `resolution` = "Promoted to `<file>` on <YYYY-MM-DD> as a lodestone: <principle>"; append "lodestone" to `seed.tags` only if not already present (idempotent).
4. Resolve: set `seed.status = SeedStatus.RESOLVED` and `seed.resolved_at = now_utc()` UNLESS `--no-resolve` was passed. Mirror the existing `resolve` command (src/seeds/cli.py, ~line 663). Persist with `db.update_seed(seed)`.
5. Echo a confirmation showing BOTH ends of the link (the file path + the appended bullet, and the seed's new resolution). Use `now_utc()` from seeds.models; render dates as YYYY-MM-DD.

Register the command on the `main` Click group, next to `resolve` / `abandon`.

## Tests (add to tests/test_cli.py; mirror the test_resolve_* tests — CliRunner + the `env_with_seeds` fixture)
- Promoting appends a bullet to a FRESH file, creating the `## Lodestones` section; the file exists and contains the principle text.
- Appending to a file that ALREADY has the section does not duplicate the heading (exactly one occurrence of the heading string).
- The appended bullet contains the seed ID and a YYYY-MM-DD date.
- The promoted seed's `resolution` names the target file path.
- The seed gains a `lodestone` tag; promoting an already-tagged seed does not duplicate the tag.
- The seed is RESOLVED by default; with `--no-resolve` the status is unchanged.
- Promoting a nonexistent seed id exits non-zero.
- `seeds list --tag lodestone` surfaces the promoted seed. NOTE: `list --tag` ALREADY EXISTS (src/seeds/cli.py `list_seeds` + `db.list_seeds`) — this is a VERIFY-only assertion; do NOT build tag filtering.

## Acceptance
- `uv run pytest tests/test_cli.py -k promote` passes.
- `uv run seeds promote --help` exits 0 and shows `--to`, `--as`, `--no-resolve`, and `--section`.
- Full suite green: `uv run pytest`.

Source: seeds-147.4 (build spec), seeds-147.3 (locked decisions), seeds-152.5 (the verb/skill cut).
notes: Design picks: (1) Factored the pure find-or-create-section + append-bullet helper into a NEW module src/seeds/lodestone.py (bead offered 'export.py OR a small helper module' — chose dedicated module since export.py is JSONL-specific). (2) promote creates missing parent dirs of --to (mkdir parents=True,exist_ok=True); bead said 'create the file' but was silent on parent dirs — chose to make 'write wherever --to points' just work. (3) The tag-surfacing test promotes with --no-resolve so the literal 'seeds list --tag lodestone' surfaces it, because promote resolves by default and list excludes terminal seeds unless --all.
close_reason: Implemented `seeds promote` verb + pure lodestone.py section helper + 8 tests; full suite green, ruff/mypy clean

title: Add seeds suggest <text> command for dedup-during-ingest
description:
## Why

When incorporating candidate items from a transcript, Claude needs to ask 'does a seed about this already exist?' for each item. `seeds search` requires guessing the right FTS5 keyword. `seeds list` is unranked. There's no purpose-built primitive.

Source: seeds-142.1, seeds-2, seeds-130.

## What

`seeds suggest <text>` returns top-N seeds ranked by relevance to the natural-language text.

Ranking (cheap, no embeddings):
- FTS5 score over title + content (tokenize the input)
- Boost by tag overlap (extract candidate tags from input)
- Optional small boost for recently-updated

Output: `id status title [tags]` plus a top matched snippet per result.

## Flags

- `--limit=N` (default 5)
- `--include-resolved` (default off)
- `--json` for agent piping

## Acceptance
- `seeds suggest 'venn diagram for comparing code sets'` on CSC returns csc-111 and csc-101.x at the top
- Performance: < 200ms on a 100-seed project
- JSON mode emits valid JSON of id/title/status/tags/snippet/score
notes: Design decisions 2026-05-18: (1) default INCLUDES resolved/abandoned — 'does this idea exist in our deliberation history' framing. Add --open-only to restrict to non-terminal. (2) Dynamic min-relevance floor: drop hits below ~half the top score. (3) Ship --json mode for agent piping.
close_reason: Implemented seeds suggest <text> with FTS5 BM25 + multiplicative tag/recency boosts and dynamic noise floor (top/2). --limit, --open-only, --json flags. Includes resolved/abandoned by default per design decision. 24 tests cover tokenizer, ranking blend, noise floor, terminal handling, JSON mode. Live CSC validation: narrow venn query returns csc-111 (bullseye); broader compare query returns full csc-101.x family — ranking blend behaving as designed.

title: Add project digest to seeds prime output
description:
## Why

Static `seeds prime` text gives Claude zero overview of existing seeds. In CSC (96 seeds), Claude issues 3-6 discovery commands per session before it can act. A digest replaces those commands with zero round-trips.

Source: seeds-87 (Dynamic prime), seeds-142 (transcript-incorporation workflow).

## What

`seeds prime` adds a `## Current Seeds` section after the workflow text:
- Total counts (open, by status)
- Recently Updated (top N by updated_at, default N=20)
- Active Exploration (status=exploring, all)
- Open Questions (type=question + status=open|captured, all)
- Tag clusters with counts (top 15)

Each row: `id status title [tags]` — no body content (Claude can `seeds show` for detail).

## Flags

- `--no-digest` — opt out for noise-sensitive sessions
- `--digest-limit=N` — cap recent-updated entries (default 20)

## Acceptance
- `seeds prime` on CSC outputs workflow text + digest
- `seeds prime --no-digest` outputs only workflow text (backwards-compat)
- Digest is < 100 lines on a 100-seed project
- Empty project: no digest section (or '0 seeds — start with `seeds jot`')
close_reason: Implemented prime digest: counts, Recently Updated (configurable limit), Active Exploration, Open Questions, Top Tag Clusters. --no-digest opts out. Backward-compatible default of include_digest=False when no db is passed, so non-CLI callers don't break. 5 new CLI tests cover digest presence, --no-digest, empty project, --digest-limit, exploration section.

title: rename-prefix should also rewrite ID references inside seed bodies
description:
The prefix rename in seeds-5at only updated the `id` column and relationship endpoints. Seed text fields (title, content, resolution) can also contain ID references like 'see seeds-7' or markdown links, which become stale after a rename.

## Changes
- New helper `rewrite_id_refs(text, old_prefix, new_prefix) -> (new_text, count)` using a tight regex with non-identifier boundary checks: `(?<![a-zA-Z0-9-])<old>-\\d+(?:\\.\\d+)*(?![a-zA-Z0-9-])`
- `Database.rename_prefix(..., rewrite_bodies=True)` walks every seed and rewrites refs in title/content/resolution
- CLI `seeds rename-prefix` defaults to rewriting; `--no-rewrite-bodies` opts out
- Auto-derive on first command uses default (rewrite=True)
- Output reports both ID and body-ref counts

## Acceptance
- 'see seeds-7' becomes 'see myproj-7' after rename
- 'seeds-related' stays untouched
- Child refs like 'seeds-7.1.2' rewrite correctly
- Markdown link form [seeds-7](...) rewrites
- Running rename twice is idempotent
- --no-rewrite-bodies disables the body sweep
close_reason: Implemented body-text rewrite for rename-prefix with --dry-run and --no-rewrite-bodies flags. Tight regex matches whole-word ID refs (preserves seeds-related etc.). Auto-derive removed entirely per follow-up. 285 tests pass.

title: Configurable project prefix for seed IDs (replace hardcoded 'seeds-N')
description:
Every seeds database currently hardcodes 'seeds' as the ID prefix (e.g., seeds-1, seeds-2.1). This means every project's IDs look identical, defeating the readability benefit of sequential IDs across multiple projects.

## What changes
- Add a persistent project prefix stored in a new \`config\` table (key/value) inside the SQLite DB
- \`seeds init\` accepts \`--prefix <name>\`; default is current directory name, sanitized to lowercase kebab-case
- \`seeds rename-prefix <new>\` command rewrites all IDs (top-level + children + relationships) to use the new prefix and re-exports JSONL
- Auto-derive on first command after upgrade: if existing DB has no prefix configured, derive from project dir name, set config, and rewrite IDs accordingly
- \`next_id()\` reads the prefix from config (no longer uses the DEFAULT_PREFIX constant for normal operation)
- Helper \`sanitize_prefix(name)\` validates and normalizes prefix strings: lowercase, replace non-alphanumeric runs with hyphens, strip leading/trailing hyphens, must start with letter

## Acceptance
- Fresh \`seeds init\` in a directory named 'My Project' sets prefix to 'my-project'
- Existing DB with seeds-N IDs auto-migrates on next command (renames + sets config)
- \`seeds rename-prefix newproj\` renames all IDs (including children like seeds-7.1 → newproj-7.1) and rewrites relationships
- All existing tests pass; new tests cover sanitize, init flag, rename-prefix, auto-derive
- \`seeds rename-prefix\` validates the new prefix and rejects empty/invalid input
close_reason: Implemented: config-backed project prefix with sanitize_prefix, init --prefix, rename-prefix command, auto-derive on first command. 260 tests pass (216 existing + 44 new).

title: feat: migrate existing hex IDs to sequential IDs
description:
One-time migration to remap all existing hex-hash IDs to sequential IDs. This is the only seeds database — no need to handle old hex IDs in import after migration.

## What this involves

### Migration strategy
1. Query all seeds ordered by created_at
2. Assign sequential IDs (seeds-1, seeds-2, ...) in creation order
3. Build an old-to-new ID mapping
4. Update all references:
   - seeds.id (primary key)
   - Parent references (child IDs like seed-81a4.1 become seeds-N.M)
   - relationships table (source_id, target_id)
   - FTS index (rebuild after migration)
5. Set the sequential counter to max + 1

### Edge cases
- Children must keep their parent relationship: if seed-81a4 becomes seeds-42, then seed-81a4.1 becomes seeds-42.1
- Relationships reference IDs — all source_id and target_id must be updated
- JSONL export should be regenerated after migration

### Safety
- Back up the DB before migration
- Run in a transaction so it's atomic
- Provide a CLI command: `seeds migrate-ids`
- Migration should be idempotent (detect if already migrated)

### Post-migration cleanup
- Remove hex ID support from import code (no backwards compat needed)
- The v1 import path can be removed or simplified since all future JSONL will have sequential IDs
close_reason: Migration complete: 163 seeds remapped from hex to sequential IDs. Children, relationships, and FTS all updated.

title: feat: add resolution text field to seeds

Add a first-class 'resolution' field to capture what happened when a seed reaches a terminal state (resolved or abandoned). Currently resolve just flips status with no record of the outcome, and abandon hacks a reason into the content field.

## Implementation Plan

### 1. Model (src/seeds/models.py)
- Add `resolution: str = ""` to the Seed dataclass (after resolved_at)

### 2. DB Schema (src/seeds/db.py)
- Add `resolution TEXT DEFAULT ''` column to SCHEMA
- Add migration: ALTER TABLE seeds ADD COLUMN resolution TEXT DEFAULT '' (for existing DBs)
- Update `_row_to_seed()` to read resolution column
- Update `create_seed()` INSERT to include resolution
- Update `update_seed()` UPDATE to include resolution
- Add resolution to FTS schema and triggers so resolved outcomes are searchable
- Update `rebuild_fts()` to include resolution

### 3. CLI (src/seeds/cli.py)
- `seeds resolve <id> --resolution/-r "what happened"` — writes to resolution field
- `seeds abandon <id> --reason/-r "why"` — writes to resolution field instead of appending to content
- Both should work without the flag (resolution is optional, not required)

### 4. Display

- `seeds prime`: include resolution in AI context output for resolved seeds

### 5. Export (src/seeds/export.py)

- Handle resolution field in JSONL import (default to empty string if missing for backwards compat)

### 6. Tests
- Test resolve with and without --resolution flag
- Test abandon writes to resolution field (not content)
- Test show displays resolution
- Test export/import round-trips resolution
- Test FTS finds seeds by resolution text
- Test migration adds column to existing DB without data loss

title: seeds-to-beads must write structured `Source:` seed lineage into every bead
description:
Make seed->bead lineage a structured field rather than prose, so recovering it is
deterministic instead of a text-matching heuristic.

From seeds-187's resolution: "What a better bead would have said: either make seeds-to-beads
write a real Source field, or specify that candidates are verified against the code rather
than against bead status." Both are needed, at different scopes — see the companion bead
seeds-20v, which fixes recovery for the 149 beads that already exist. This bead prevents
recurrence for beads written from now on.

## The problem

`resolve-seeds-from-beads` recovers which seeds a bead came from by text-matching seed IDs
mentioned in prose inside bead descriptions. That over-claims: a bead that merely mentions a
seed is indistinguishable from one that implements it. Observed failure, 2026-08-31:
seeds-lcfa.1.1 reported shipped because seeds-ww8 mentioned it and closed, when seeds-ww8
had actually shipped a different downstream fix.

Prose lineage cannot be made reliable by better matching. The fix is to stop inferring it.

## The change

`seeds-to-beads` must write the originating seed IDs into a structured, machine-readable
field on each bead it creates — distinguishing seeds the bead IMPLEMENTS from seeds merely
cited for context. The distinction is the point: today both look identical.

Determine the right mechanism against the beads CLI as it actually is (a labelled field, a
dedicated section with a fixed header, or `bd`'s own metadata affordances if one fits).
Verify with `bd` before choosing; do not assume a `Source:` field exists just because
seeds-187 named one.

## Relationship to seeds-152.5

This is the ratified test applied: recovering lineage is DETERMINISTIC, so it should not
depend on a model re-reading prose. The skill decides which seeds are implemented; recording
that decision in a recoverable form is mechanism.

## Scope

`src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/skills/seeds-to-beads/SKILL.md`, plus the corresponding
read side of resolve-seeds-from-beads so it prefers the structured field when present and
falls back to code verification (seeds-20v) when absent.

## Out of scope

- Backfilling lineage onto the 149 existing closed beads. seeds-20v covers those by
  verifying against code instead.

## Acceptance

- Beads created by seeds-to-beads carry structured lineage distinguishing implements-vs-cites.
- resolve-seeds-from-beads prefers that field and falls back to code verification.
- The mechanism was verified against the real `bd` CLI, and the PR says which was chosen and why.
- pytest and `seeds check` green.
design: seeds-152.5 applied: lineage recovery is deterministic and must not depend on re-reading prose. Companion to seeds-20v, which handles the 149 pre-existing beads a new field cannot reach.
acceptance_criteria: seeds-to-beads writes machine-readable seed lineage on each bead it creates, distinguishing implemented seeds from cited ones; resolve-seeds-from-beads prefers that field and falls back to code verification when absent; the chosen mechanism verified against the real bd CLI and justified in the PR; pytest and seeds check green.

title: Add the `winnow` skill: judge corpus-audit candidates and present findings
description:
The judgment half of `winnow`. A Claude Code skill in the seeds plugin that runs
`seeds winnow --json`, judges the scoped candidates, and presents findings for the user to
rule on. Depends on the `seeds winnow` verb bead; must not reimplement detection.

Deliberation: seeds-158 (resolved umbrella), seeds-159, seeds-164 (detection rule),
seeds-163 (formalize as skill-over-verb), seeds-152.5.

## Scope — ONE file

`src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/skills/winnow/SKILL.md`. No Python changes.

## What it does

1. Runs `seeds winnow --json`.
2. Passes HARD findings through essentially unedited — they are facts (quiet deferrals,
   blocked-but-unblocked, long-unresolved). No judgment is needed and none should be added.
3. Judges SOFT candidates: is this edge pair genuinely contradictory, or merely two related
   seeds that agree? Has this premise actually aged out, or is the seed just old?
4. Presents findings for the user to rule on, then applies the rulings (resolve, abandon,
   link, append a correction).

## The three rules that make this trustworthy

1. **Hard and soft findings stay in separate sections of the report.** A speculative
   staleness guess must never sit in the same list as a factual one; one bad soft finding
   would otherwise discredit the whole report.
2. **Every finding cites its evidence** — the specific seed IDs and the specific conflicting
   text. A finding that cannot cite is not reported. No "this cluster feels stale."
3. **"Nothing to report" is a good outcome.** Never pad with marginal findings to look
   productive. Most passes over a healthy corpus should be short.

The failure mode being defended against: a corpus auditor that cries wolf is worse than no
auditor, because it trains the reader to skip it. Ryan ruled all five flavors in scope
having heard this objection, so the guard lives in the report's shape.

## The five flavors (all in scope)

- **Contradiction** — the sharpest, and the one with a proof case: seeds-74.2.1 vs
  seeds-74.2.2 contradicted each other for six months. Judge the verb's edge pairs.
- **Neglected deferrals** — hard, pass through.
- **Long-unresolved / blocked-but-unblocked** — hard, pass through.
- **Staleness** — judge only candidates citing a checkable premise. Age alone is NOT
  staleness; saying otherwise is how this becomes the decay-detection engine seeds-159
  warned against.
- **Outcome and learning** — surfaced as questions FOR THE USER, never asserted. Neither is
  detectable from the corpus (seeds-164).

## Frontmatter

`description` is the trigger. Write it to match how this gets asked: "audit the seeds",
"anything contradictory in here?", "what's gone stale?", "go through the backlog",
"winnow the corpus". Match the voice of the existing skills.

## Relationship to its siblings

- `glean` works the field: transcripts in, new seeds out.
- `winnow` works the barn: the existing corpus in, attention out.
- `cutting` parks a live topic mid-conversation.
Say this in the skill so the three do not bleed into each other.

## Acceptance

- SKILL.md exists, picked up by `seeds skills install`.
- Calls `seeds winnow --json`; does not reimplement detection or scan the corpus itself.
- Hard/soft separation and evidence citation are explicit instructions in the skill text.
- pytest and `seeds check` green; no new subcommand from this bead.
design: Judgment half of the hybrid ruled in seeds-158/163 per seeds-152.5. All five flavors in scope by Ryan's ruling; the crying-wolf risk is managed by report shape (hard/soft separation, mandatory citation, no padding) rather than by narrowing scope.
acceptance_criteria: A single SKILL.md at src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/skills/winnow/SKILL.md that consumes seeds winnow --json rather than scanning the corpus itself; hard findings passed through unedited and kept in a section separate from judged soft findings; every finding cites seed IDs and conflicting text; 'nothing to report' explicitly framed as a good outcome; picked up by seeds skills install; pytest and seeds check green.

title: Add the `seeds winnow` CLI verb: mechanical corpus-audit findings and candidate scoping
description:
The deterministic half of `winnow`, the corpus-audit command. Walks the seed graph and
emits (a) hard findings that need no judgment, and (b) scoped candidate sets for the skill
to judge. Calls no model.

Deliberation: seeds-158 (resolved umbrella, all five flavors), seeds-159 (staleness +
contradiction), seeds-164 (the detection rule), seeds-162 (neglected deferrals),
seeds-163 (formalize as a command), seeds-152.5 (deterministic -> verb).

## The boundary this command sits on

- `seeds check`  — are the FILES valid?      (format rules)
- `seeds doctor` — is the STORE healthy?     (operational: dangling edges, prefixes)
- `seeds winnow` — is the THINKING healthy?  (semantic: contradiction, staleness, neglect)

Do NOT fold this into check or doctor. That boundary is currently clean and seeds-163
explicitly rejected overloading them.

## THE detection rule — read this before designing anything

**Contradictions live inside clusters, not across the corpus.** Contradiction requires two
seeds to be about the same thing, and parent/child plus `relates-to` edges already encode
exactly that. The candidate set is the EDGE SET, not the cross product.

Measured 2026-09-01: 314 seeds, 692 edges. That is ~692 comparisons, not ~49,000. The unit
of review is an edge, not a seed. Do not implement corpus-wide pairwise scanning, and do not
implement sampling.

## What the verb emits

**Hard findings (facts — no judgment, fully testable):**
- Neglected deferrals: deferred and untouched since <date>.
- Blocked-but-unblocked: status blocked while every blocker is now closed.
- Long-unresolved: exploring/captured well past a threshold, with graph position.

**Scoped candidates (for the skill to judge — the verb only narrows, never concludes):**
- Contradiction candidates: edge pairs where both endpoints are resolved, or one resolved
  and the other captured later. Emit both endpoints' relevant text.
- Staleness candidates: resolved seeds citing a CHECKABLE premise — a version, a
  measurement, a data shape. NOT seeds that are merely old. Age alone is not evidence of
  staleness and must not be treated as such (seeds-159's stated risk).
- Outcome / learning candidates: resolved seeds with downstream beads or implementation
  links. These cannot be detected from the corpus and are surfaced as prompts only.

Output must keep hard findings and scoped candidates in SEPARATE sections. A soft-flavor
false positive must not be able to discredit the factual section.

## Surface

`seeds winnow [--flavor=<name>...] [--since=<date>] [--json]`

Default runs all flavors. `--json` for the skill to consume.

## Testing the detector (non-negotiable)

A stale-check is itself code that can be silently wrong. Hand-built fixture corpora with
hand-computed expected answers. Required cases:
- A true intra-cluster contradiction -> detected.
- **Two related seeds that AGREE -> NOT flagged.** This is the crying-wolf test and it is
  the most important one in the suite.
- A deferred-and-quiet seed -> flagged; a deferred-but-recently-touched seed -> not.
- A blocked seed whose blockers are all closed -> flagged.
- An old resolved seed with no checkable premise -> NOT flagged as stale.
Do not read the real ~/.claude or the project's own .seeds in tests.

## Out of scope

- Any judgment about whether a candidate is genuinely contradictory (that is the skill).
- Writing or mutating seeds. This verb is read-only.
- `thresh` as a separate command.

## Acceptance

- `seeds winnow` in `seeds --help`; read-only; hard and soft output separated; `--json` works.
- Detection walks edges, not the cross product.
- pytest covers every case above, including the agree-but-related false-positive case.
- pytest and `seeds check` green.
design: Detection rule from seeds-164: contradictions live inside clusters, so the candidate set is the 692-edge graph, not ~49,000 pairs. Ryan ruled all five flavors in scope over a contradiction-only first cut, so the crying-wolf guard moved from scope into shape: hard/soft separation, mandatory evidence citation, and a tested false-positive path.
acceptance_criteria: seeds winnow exists, is read-only, walks the edge set rather than the seed cross product, and separates hard findings from scoped candidates; --json consumable by the skill; pytest covers the true-contradiction, agreeing-pair (false positive), quiet-deferral, unblocked-blocked and old-but-not-stale cases on fixture corpora; pytest and seeds check green.

title: Add the `glean` skill: judge and present candidates from `seeds glean`
description:
The judgment half of `glean`. A Claude Code skill in the seeds plugin that runs
`seeds glean`, decides which of its candidates are real, and presents them for review.

Depends on the `seeds glean` CLI verb bead — this skill calls it and must not reimplement
extraction.

Deliberation: seeds-74.2 (resolved: capture is hybrid), seeds-74.2.1 (design),
seeds-74.2.2 (why it must not analyse the model's own context), seeds-152.5 (ratified:
judgment -> skill).

## Scope — ONE file

`src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/skills/glean/SKILL.md`. No Python changes; all mechanics
live in the verb.

## Critical constraint: never glean from your own context

The skill MUST invoke `seeds glean` and reason over its output. It must NOT summarize the
conversation from the model's own context instead. Post-compaction context is summarized
and loses exact figures, verbatim user quotes, and things mentioned-but-not-acted-on —
exactly the set glean exists to recover. The failure is silent and shape-dependent: it
looks fine in short sessions and fails in the long ones that need it most. This mistake was
the standing conclusion in seeds-74.2.2 for six months before being overturned; say so in
the skill so it is not reintroduced.

## Behaviour

- Runs `seeds glean` for the current session.
- Judges each candidate: is this real deliberation worth keeping, or noise? Most raw
  candidates will not be worth a seed.
- Presents survivors for review, one at a time, y/n/edit. Suggest-and-review is the
  default; never create unattended in the interactive path.
- Writes accepted candidates with `seeds create`, linking them to related existing seeds.
- Reports plainly when nothing was missed. "Nothing to glean" is a good outcome and must
  not be padded with marginal candidates to look productive.

## Frontmatter

`description` is the trigger — the harness matches it against user intent, so there is no
magic phrase. Write it to match how this is actually asked: "what did we miss?",
"glean this session", "anything not captured?", "land the plane". Match the voice of the
existing skills (feedback, trellis, seeds-to-beads, resolve-seeds-from-beads,
cutting).

## Relationship to `cutting`

Siblings, not overlaps: `cutting` is the proactive in-conversation half, `glean` the
retrospective end-of-session half (seeds-74.2). A gleaned candidate that deserves its own
thread is a cutting; say so in the skill.

## Out of scope

- Extraction logic (the verb owns it).
- Non-Claude-Code sources (seeds-74.2.4, rejected pivot).
- Requiring marker phrases — hints only, never a dependency (seeds-74.2.3).

## Acceptance

- SKILL.md exists and is picked up by `seeds skills install` alongside the others.
- The skill calls `seeds glean` rather than reasoning over the raw conversation.
- pytest green, `seeds check` clean, no new subcommand from this bead.
design: Judgment half of the hybrid ruled in seeds-74.2.1 per seeds-152.5. The load-bearing constraint is that it must read the verb's output, not the model's compacted context -- seeds-74.2.2 held the opposite conclusion for six months and it was wrong.
acceptance_criteria: A single SKILL.md at src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/skills/glean/SKILL.md that invokes the seeds glean verb rather than summarizing from the model's own context; suggest-and-review by default; picked up by seeds skills install; pytest and seeds check green; no Python changes in this bead.

title: Add the `seeds glean` CLI verb: extract seed candidates from a session transcript
description:
The deterministic half of `glean` (formerly `sweep`). Resolves a Claude Code session
transcript, extracts candidate deliberation, diffs it against the existing corpus, and
emits a compact candidate list. The judgment half is a separate skill (see the dependent
bead); this bead adds NO prompting and calls no model.

Deliberation: seeds-74.2 (resolved: capture is hybrid), seeds-74.2.1 (the design),
seeds-74.2.4 (why the name is `glean`), seeds-152.5 (ratified: deterministic -> verb).

## Why a verb and not just letting the skill read the file

Two independent reasons, both settled in seeds-74.2.1:
1. Cost. Measured on titan 2026-09-01: one ordinary working session's JSONL is 502KB /
   256 turns. Handing that to a model raw to find a handful of gaps is the wrong shape.
2. Testability. A verb gets pytest coverage; a skill gets none.

## Session resolution — do NOT write a heuristic

`$CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID` is present in the agent's environment and resolves directly to
`~/.claude/projects/<project-slug>/<session-id>.jsonl`. Verified on titan 2026-09-01.
There is no need for most-recently-modified guessing, and it must not be added.
The project slug is the cwd path with `/` replaced by `-` (e.g.
`/home/ryan/projects/outins/seeds` -> `-home-ryan-projects-outins-seeds`).

## Surface

`seeds glean [--session=ID] [--all] [--auto] [--force] [--since=<date>]`

- default: current session from the env var
- `--session=ID`: a specific session
- `--all`: every transcript for this project (historical pass)
- `--since=<date>`: bound a historical pass
- `--force`: re-glean a transcript already marked gleaned
- `--auto`: see below

## Behaviour

1. Resolve transcript path(s).
2. Parse user + assistant turns. Skip already-gleaned transcripts unless `--force`.
3. Emit candidates: questions raised (answered or not), decisions made with rationale,
   data discoveries with specific figures, user clarifications, and question->answer->
   decision chains.
4. Cross-reference against the existing corpus so things already captured are not offered
   again.
5. Print a compact candidate list. Filtering happens HERE — the consumer must never receive
   the raw transcript.

Marker phrases ("Tangent:", "Decision:", "TODO:") are treated as strong signals where they
appear, but must NOT be required and nothing may depend on them (seeds-74.2.3).

## --auto

Ryan ruled 2026-09-01 that `--auto` stays as an opt-in for bulk historical passes.
Guardrail that ruling requires: seeds created under `--auto` MUST be distinguishable
afterwards — tag them — so an unattended pass can be audited or reverted without
hand-sorting it out of a 314-file corpus. Default remains suggest-and-review.

## Re-glean tracking

Record which transcripts have been gleaned so repeat runs skip them by default and
re-gleaning is deliberate. Choose the simplest durable place for this marker and state the
choice in the PR.

## Out of scope

- The skill that judges candidates (separate bead, depends on this one).
- Any non-Claude-Code source: no --email, --slack, --stdin. The source-agnostic pivot was
  rejected and stays rejected (seeds-74.2.4).
- `thresh` / `winnow` as commands.

## Acceptance

- `seeds glean` appears in `seeds --help` with the flags above.
- pytest covers: session resolution from the env var, parse, corpus diff, already-gleaned
  skip, and `--force` override. Use fixture transcripts; do not read the real ~/.claude.
- `uv run pytest` green, `uv run seeds check` clean.
design: Hybrid shape ruled in seeds-74.2.1 per seeds-152.5: deterministic extraction is a tested CLI verb, judgment is a separate skill. Reads the transcript rather than the model's context because post-compaction context loses exact figures, verbatim quotes and mentioned-but-unacted items -- precisely what glean exists to recover.
acceptance_criteria: seeds glean exists with the documented flags; resolves the transcript from $CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID with no most-recently-modified heuristic; emits a filtered candidate list rather than raw transcript; pytest covers resolution, parse, corpus diff, gleaned-skip and --force using fixture transcripts; pytest and seeds check green.
notes:
Design picks made under the 2-way-choice ruling (code-only), 2026-09-02:

1. GLEANED MARKER LIVES AT .seeds/gleaned.jsonl. One JSON object per gleaned
   transcript, appended: {session, gleaned_at, candidates, created}. Beside
   config.yaml as repo-level state (storage-format §9), NOT inside
   .seeds/seeds/, so Store.records() never sees it and seeds check has nothing
   to say about it. §8's ban on derived artifacts does not reach it: nothing in
   it is computed from the seed files, so there is no second copy of anything
   that could disagree with them. Rejected: a key in config.yaml (read_config
   is flat key:value, a growing list does not fit) and a marker beside the
   transcript in ~/.claude (not durable, not in the repo, lost on a reclone).

2. --since on a --all pass filters by transcript FILE MTIME, not by the
   transcript's own first/last timestamp. Reading 300 files to decide which 300
   files to read is the worse trade.

3. SIDECHAIN TURNS ARE SKIPPED. A sub-agent's conversation is a different
   session's deliberation and has its own transcript; isMeta entries are
   harness bookkeeping.

4. THE SPEAKER RULE (the substantive one, and it is measured). Classifying user
   and assistant turns alike produced 475 candidates / 82KB from this project's
   own 5.3MB, 251-turn transcript — 247 of them 'decisions' — i.e. a filtered
   transcript rather than a candidate list. A decision is a commitment and the
   assistant's prose is a report of work written in the same modal voice, so
   phrase matching cannot separate them. The assistant now contributes only a
   figure it measured, a line it marked, and a question ending its turn. Result
   on the same transcript: 96 candidates / 13KB. Nothing DEPENDS on markers —
   every user-side rule and two of the three assistant rules work with zero
   markers in the file; a marker only rescues an assistant line.

5. A FIGURE ALONE IS NOT A MEASUREMENT. Requires a comparison shape (83 of 306,
   65 -> 385) or a measurement verb beside the figure. A figure-only rule made
   198 of 301 candidates ('doctor green at 312 seeds' is in most turns).

6. CORPUS DIFF IS PER BODY LINE, not against the whole body. Containment >= 0.8
   of the candidate's content words in one line, >= 4 tokens. Scored against a
   whole 4000-word body, containment suppresses nearly anything — and a
   suppressed real gap leaves nothing on screen to say so.

7. NO --json on glean. Not in the ruled surface; the consumer is a skill that
   reads prose.

title: Add the `cutting` skill: context-carrying capture of a mid-conversation topic
description:
Ship a new Claude Code skill, `cutting`, in the seeds plugin. It is the vegetative sibling
of `seeds jot`: where a jot captures a topic's STATEMENT, a cutting captures the topic
together with enough surrounding deliberation to resume it cold in a later session.

## Why

In a long-running session several distinct topics surface, each warranting its own thread.
Working one means the others fall by the wayside — not rejected, just unheld. A one-line
jot loses the argument that made the topic worth raising, so restarting from it is a cold
start, and that cost is why parked topics stay parked.

Deliberation: seeds-h5rq (the command and its naming), seeds-h5rq.1 (ruled: carry an
excerpt, not a session pointer), seeds-h5rq.2 (why the harness's own /fork does not solve
it), seeds-h5rq.3 (ruled: pure skill, zero new CLI surface).

## Scope — ONE file

Create `src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/skills/cutting/SKILL.md`.

There is NO new CLI verb. Per seeds-152.5 (ratified: deterministic->verb, judgment->skill),
the judgment is the whole feature and the mechanism it needs is `seeds create --content`,
which already exists. Do not add a `seeds cutting` subcommand. Do not modify src/seeds/*.py.

## Required behaviour of the skill

- Triggers when the user wants a live side-topic set aside without losing it ("take a
  cutting", "set that aside", "park that for later").
- Writes ONE seed via `seeds create` with `--content` carrying a body rich enough to resume
  cold. The body must state: what was being discussed, why this topic matters, what the
  open question is, and what was already ruled out. A one-liner is a jot and is a failure
  of this skill.
- Includes a conversation excerpt in the body — NOT a pointer to a session id. Session ids
  are host-local and rot (seeds-h5rq.1).
- Links the new seed to the seed(s) the conversation was already about, when there are any.
- Returns to the original topic immediately. The whole point is not derailing the main
  thread; the skill must not turn into a side conversation.
- Does NOT resolve, defer, or otherwise change state on any existing seed.

## Frontmatter

Match the style of the four existing skills in that directory (feedback,
resolve-seeds-from-beads, seeds-to-beads, trellis): `name` + a `description` written so the
harness can auto-match it to user intent. Read those four first and follow their voice.

## Explicitly out of scope

- `sweep` (seeds-74.2.x) — a separate, hybrid skill+verb, and its design is not settled yet.
- Any Stop-hook that surfaces `seeds ready`.
- Any change to `jot`.

## Acceptance

- The new SKILL.md exists and `seeds skills install` picks it up alongside the other four.
- `uv run pytest` passes.
- `uv run seeds check` reports no violations.
- No new subcommand appears in `seeds --help`.
design: Ruled in seeds-h5rq.3 by the test ratified in seeds-152.5: judgment->skill, deterministic->CLI verb. cutting is pure judgment, so it is a skill with zero new binary surface, unlike sweep which is a hybrid.
acceptance_criteria: A single new SKILL.md at src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/skills/cutting/SKILL.md; no new CLI subcommand; no changes under src/seeds/*.py; pytest green; seeds check clean; the skill is picked up by seeds skills install.

title: seeds validated a bead ref against a stale .beads/issues.jsonl and rejected a real id
description:
Found 2026-09-01. Referencing a just-created bead id from a seed body was REJECTED, and clearing it needed --allow-unknown-refs, which disables ALL ref validation including the hallucinated-seed-id detection the check exists for. @aguynamedryan: "seeds needs to be able to append bead refs without need to allow unknown refs, which opens us up to hallucination again."

ROOT CAUSE, verified: the validator already knows about beads - prime documents that "existing seeds, beads (from a sibling .beads/issues.jsonl) and a short allowlist of prose terms all count as known". It was not missing the feature; it read a STALE export. bd create writes to Dolt, and the JSONL export is throttled (export.interval, default 60s), so the sibling file had not caught up. Re-running the identical update minutes later succeeded with no override.

So the bug is that seeds validates against a DERIVED, THROTTLED artifact and treats its absence as authoritative. That is precisely the class this storage overhaul just removed from seeds itself - a stale derived store trusted as truth - still present here because the derived store belongs to beads.

Two directions, needs a pick: consult beads directly (bd is on PATH; authoritative, but adds a subprocess dependency to a hot path), or keep reading the JSONL and degrade honestly - when an unknown ref matches the sibling bead prefix, say the bead list may be stale rather than flatly rejecting.

Worth noting the escape hatch is also too coarse: --allow-unknown-refs is all-or-nothing, so using it for one legitimate bead ref disables hallucination detection for the whole edit.

Source: seeds-142.3
acceptance_criteria: Creating a bead and immediately referencing its id from a seed body succeeds without --allow-unknown-refs. If the beads export cannot be trusted to be current, the validator either consults beads directly or reports that its bead list may be stale rather than calling a real id unknown.
notes:
RULED (@aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01): "I think just introducing beads validation of refs (if beads is in use) solves the entire problem (other than beads/seeds ids look interchangeable to a user, but I am fine with that for now)."

One correction to the framing, which changes what to build: the validation is NOT missing. seeds prime documents it, and it was verified working - the exact update that got rejected succeeded minutes later with no override once the export caught up. What fails is that it reads .beads/issues.jsonl, a THROTTLED DERIVED EXPORT, and treats a miss there as authoritative.

So the work is to make the existing check trustworthy, not to add one. His "if beads is in use" is the right guard: only apply bead-ref validation when a sibling .beads/ exists.

This also settles the scope question the bead left open. With bead refs validating reliably, --allow-unknown-refs stops being reached for routinely, so its all-or-nothing coarseness is no longer urgent - note it, do not redesign it.

And it closes out the id-collision thread: the look-alike ids stay for now, by ruling ("I am fine with that for now"). The tilde change is deferred to P3 pending seeds-32ai.
PICKED (a): consult beads directly via `bd show <ids> --json`, guarded by a sibling .beads/config.yaml (the marker bd init writes) and bd being on PATH.

Why not (b) degrade-and-allow: this repo's seeds prefix and beads prefix are BOTH "seeds", so "unknown ref matching the bead prefix" is EVERY hallucinated seed id. Warning-and-allowing there would retire the hallucination check exactly where it matters most. (b) is also unreachable in the reproduced case - there was no .beads/issues.jsonl at all, so there was no bead prefix to match against.

Cost control, so (a) does not put a subprocess on the hot path: the JSONL is still read first and answers nearly every lookup; bd is asked ONLY about refs the export did not vouch for, i.e. only on the path that was about to error. A body whose refs all resolve never spawns anything, and neither does a project with no .beads/config.yaml.

`bd show` rather than `bd list --id`: list applies the default status filter (a CLOSED bead comes back missing - verified) and hides gate/infra/template beads. show fetches by id with no filtering.

Kept from (b) as a fallback, not a substitute: when beads IS in use but bd cannot be reached (not on PATH, crash, timeout, unparseable output), the rejection now says the bead list came from a throttled export that may be stale, instead of implying it was complete. query_bead_ids returns None for that case and set() for bd authoritatively saying "no issues found" - the two are never collapsed.
close_reason: bead refs are now validated against bd itself: the throttled JSONL export answers first, and bd show is consulted only for refs it could not vouch for, gated on a sibling .beads/config.yaml and bd being on PATH; could-not-consult and authoritatively-absent are never collapsed, so hallucinated seed ids are still rejected

title: Detect a seed body rewritten in place: content differs from HEAD while updated_at did not
description:
Filed 2026-09-01 by the agent that built seeds-4co.16, correcting a premise that was mine and was half wrong.

I claimed the non-canonical-bytes smell was "the positive assertion that catches whatever tool nobody predicted -- it notices that a seed WAS REWRITTEN, whichever tool did it". Measured, it is only half true. The comparison is the file against render_seed_file(what the file NOW says), i.e. a render of itself. So it catches SERIALIZATION drift -- an extra trailing newline, blank lines around the body, reordered frontmatter keys -- and is blind to any rewrite of the body text that leaves the layout canonical.

The motivating case falls in the blind spot. ruff 0.16 reformatting a Python code block inside a seed body produces a file that is still perfectly canonical; only the prose changed. Trimming trailing whitespace off a body line is the same shape. Both directions are now pinned by tests in seeds-4co.16, including test_a_body_rewritten_within_canonical_layout_is_NOT_caught.

So the tooling-scope defence (seeds-dv6r) rests on two rules, not one, and only one of them exists:
- tool-config-includes-store catches the tools we can NAME (shipped in seeds-4co.16)
- non-canonical-bytes catches SERIALIZATION rewrites (shipped in seeds-4co.16)
- nothing yet catches a CONTENT rewrite that preserves layout -- this bead

THE SHAPE THAT WORKS: body differs from its committed version while updated_at is unchanged. Every legitimate edit goes through the CLI and bumps updated_at, so the pair "content moved, timestamp did not" is exactly the signature of something other than seeds writing the file. That is git-comparison territory, so it belongs with seeds check --against-git rather than in the file-local smells tier, which is why seeds-4co.16 deliberately did not build it.

Source: seeds-dv6r, seeds-4co.16, seeds-4co.5
acceptance_criteria: A seed file whose body text differs from its committed version while updated_at is unchanged is reported. A legitimate edit through the CLI (which bumps updated_at) is NOT reported. A test reproduces the ruff shape: reformat a Python code block inside a seed body, leaving frontmatter and layout canonical, and the check flags it.
notes:
RULED (@aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01): keep the rule, but only flag a body difference an ID rewrite cannot explain.

WHY IT NEEDED A RULING - verified empirically, not reasoned about. seeds rename-prefix rewrites ID references INSIDE bodies and deliberately does NOT bump updated_at (store.py:596 states the reason: a rename is not an edit to the deliberation, and bumping it corpus-wide would destroy the updated_at == created_at "never edited" test). Measured on a copy of the real store: seeds-lcfa updated_at was byte-identical before and after a rename. So the signature as filed - "body differs from HEAD while updated_at did not" - fires on EVERY seed after a sanctioned rename.

THE RULE: a body difference fully accounted for by prefix substitution (<old>-x becomes <new>-x, and nothing else changed) is silent. Any other difference is flagged. rename-prefix produces 0 findings; a formatter reflowing a code block inside a body is still caught, which is the case this exists for (bead seeds-4co.16 pinned that ruff-shaped rewrite as invisible to the canonical-bytes smell).

Rejected: making rename-prefix bump updated_at, which would simplify the rule at the cost of the never-edited signal across the whole corpus on every rename.

Implementation note: the exemption must be computed, not assumed - derive the old and new prefix from the diff itself and confirm every difference is explained, rather than trusting that a commit which touched many files was a rename.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-01 (branch seeds-4co.21/content-rewrite-detection).

TIER: --against-git, and it GATES (exit non-zero), same as mass-field-rewrite. The 2-way pick was gate-vs-report-only; gating wins because the signature is not a judgement call. 'body moved, updated_at did not' has exactly one benign producer (rename-prefix) and that one is exempted by construction, so a finding here is a positive assertion that something other than seeds wrote the file. A report-only rule would have let ruff's rewrite of seeds-154 land and be committed, which is the incident this exists to stop. Standing count on the real store is zero, so it costs nothing at commit time.

PER-SEED, NO THRESHOLD: unlike mass-field-rewrite. One file quietly reformatted is the whole incident; waiting for a fraction of the corpus means waiting for the tool to be run repo-wide a second time.

EXEMPTION, COMPUTED NOT ASSUMED: _prefix_rename() derives (old, new) from the ids that actually moved -- every departing id must carry one single prefix, the arrivals must account for them, the two must differ -- then verifies per seed with rewrite_id_refs(), the same substitution engine rename_prefix itself used, given the same known_ids. 'Explained by the rename' means reproduced byte-exactly, never 'resembles one'. Extra arrivals are tolerated (a rename and a jot can share a commit); the looseness costs nothing because the pair can only silence a diff prefix substitution reproduces exactly.

MEASURED ON THE REAL STORE (a temp copy, never the live .seeds/):
- untouched: 0 findings
- corpus-wide 'rename-prefix sprout' over all 314 seeds: 0 body-rewritten-in-place
- the same rename with one prose-shaped id (seeds-experiment) that survives it, body refs rewritten under a frozen stamp: 0 findings -- the exemption firing on real data
- a REAL 'ruff format' of the python code block in seeds-154 (the block ruff actually went for): FLAGGED, while check --smells reports 0 non-canonical-bytes on the same file, so the blind spot is closed rather than asserted.

PRE-EXISTING, NOT CHANGED BY THIS: a corpus-wide rename-prefix already trips 12 mass-field-rewrite findings, and did so before this work -- the comparison joins by id, so every renamed seed reads as a deletion. Confirmed by running it on 0.6-era code. That is the documented 'SKIP=seeds-check for an intended mass rewrite' path; out of scope here.
close_reason: body-rewritten-in-place lands in --against-git and gates: per-seed, unthresholded, with the rename exemption COMPUTED from the ids that actually moved and verified by reproducing each body byte-exactly; a real ruff reformat of seeds-154's code block is flagged while the canonical-bytes smell reports nothing on the same file, so the blind spot is demonstrated closed

title: Document the cross-repo rg recipe, and stop seeds export over-claiming
description:
Ruled by @aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01, resolving seeds-183: no single-location store, no new verb, document the recipe.

THE RECIPE, which is what 88% of real cross-repo demand actually wanted:

  rg -l "adjudicat" ~/projects/outins/*/.seeds/seeds/
  rg -i -C2 "immutable row" <habitat>/*/.seeds/seeds/

This beats what it replaces. Measured on the corpus: rg over the tree puts the seed id in the file path and gives real context lines, where grep over seeds.jsonl returned a 120-character slice of an escaped single line. Conversion is an upgrade for this workflow.

WHY IT NEEDS DOCUMENTING RATHER THAN LEAVING TO INSTINCT: the transcript evidence shows every one of those 35 invocations was a hand-rolled shell loop, reinvented each time, mostly inside habitat sessions. Nothing told the agent how to do it, so each one guessed. That is exactly the gap prime exists to close.

THE CORRECTION: seeds export --help currently says "13 repos of cross-project query depend on it". That is wrong and it is mine. The grep workflows do not depend on it and get better after conversion; roughly 2-3 of 26 real calls were structured extraction. export stays -- it is a stdout pipe, so no second store and no sync cost -- but it should describe itself as serving structured extraction (feed it to duckdb) and point at rg for search.

Source: seeds-183, seeds-4co.12
acceptance_criteria: 'seeds prime' teaches the cross-repo search recipe (rg over */.seeds/seeds/) so an agent finds it without inventing a loop. The habitat CLAUDE.md carries the same recipe. 'seeds export --help' no longer claims that cross-project query depends on it, and instead says it serves structured extraction while full-text search across repos is rg's job. No new command is added.
close_reason: prime teaches the cross-repo rg recipe as its own section with why it beats grepping the JSONL; seeds export --help now leads with structured extraction and points at ripgrep for search; the '13 repos of cross-project query depend on it' claim removed from help, module docstring and tests

title: flake.nix hand-mirrors [project.dependencies] with no gate — a dependency change can pass every check and break only the nix build
description:
flake.nix:54 carries `dependencies = with python3Packages; [ click ]`, a hand-maintained mirror of pyproject.toml's [project.dependencies]. Nothing keeps them in step. Its own comment says "Keep this list in step with [project.dependencies] — that is the whole point", which is a request, not a gate.

Found while deleting the web UI (seeds-4co.8, 2026-08-31): dropping flask from pyproject.toml left flake.nix still naming it, and the only thing that caught it was running `nix flake check --print-build-logs` by hand — about 2 minutes cold. ruff, mypy, the full pytest suite and `uv lock --check` were all green with the mismatch in place.

This is the SAME DEFECT CLASS the sibling bead seeds-3p1 just closed for uv.lock, and it is the third instance in this repo of a gate that measures something adjacent to what it claims to verify — after doctor's mtime proxy and changelog_coverage's commit count. Two artifacts derive from pyproject.toml's dependency list; one of them now has a gate and the other does not.

Note the nix job DOES run in the pre-push stage and in CI, so this is not undetected — it is detected expensively and late, at the slowest gate in the stack, where a fast comparison of two short lists would do.
acceptance_criteria: A change adding or removing a dependency in pyproject.toml without the matching flake.nix edit fails a local gate, and the gate names the mismatched dependency. Adding and removing a dep with both files in step passes. The check runs somewhere cheaper than the ~2min 'nix flake check --print-build-logs' it replaces as the detector.
notes:
RULED (@aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01): run this at the SAME point in the gate as the changelog check, not as a separate step. 'just changelog-coverage' already answers 'does the artifact match its source'; flake.nix vs pyproject.toml dependency agreement is the same shape, so it belongs as a sibling script invoked alongside it in the pre-push stage.
RULED (@aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01): run this at the SAME point in the gate as the changelog check, not as a separate step. "just changelog-coverage" already answers "does the artifact match its source"; flake.nix vs pyproject.toml dependency agreement is exactly the same shape, so it belongs as a sibling script invoked alongside it in the pre-push stage rather than as its own ceremony.
IMPLEMENTED (2026-09-01, branch seeds-8ro/flake-pyproject-gate).

RULING PREMISE CORRECTED: the ruling says to run this "at the SAME point in the gate as the changelog check ... in the pre-push stage". changelog_coverage.py is NOT a pre-push hook — it is a release-time `just changelog-coverage` / `just changelog-section` recipe, run by hand before tagging. So "the same point" was resolved as the parts of the ruling that are unambiguous: a sibling SCRIPT (scripts/flake_deps_check.py beside scripts/changelog_coverage.py), a sibling `just` recipe (`just flake-deps` beside `just changelog-coverage`), and the pre-push stage the ruling names explicitly.

PICK 1 (scope): gates [project.dependencies] ONLY. flake.nix also declares ripgrep (runtime, via makeWrapper) and git/ripgrep/pytestCheckHook (nativeCheckInputs), but NONE of them has a counterpart in pyproject.toml — they are single declarations, not duplicated ones, so there are not two lists to compare. Gating them would mean inventing a source of truth (grepping src/ for subprocess binary names), i.e. measuring a proxy — the exact defect class this bead exists to close. Recorded in the script docstring; left out until something declares them twice.

PICK 2 (wiring): its own pre-push hook, `flake-deps-check`, placed immediately ABOVE nix-pre-push rather than folded inside it. Folding it in would inherit that hook`s clean skip when nix is absent, and a contributor without nix must still be told they desynced the two files. No ci.yml counterpart on purpose: CI already catches this inside the nix job, and the pre-push contract ("if pre-push passes, CI passes") is one-directional, so an extra local check never weakens it. Noted in the section comment.

PICK 3 (interpreter): the hook runs `python3` directly, not `uv run` — the script is pure stdlib (tomllib + re), which keeps it clear of the uv re-lock ordering hazard documented on uv-lock-check. Same reasoning as git-config-sanity. The `just` recipe uses `uv run python` to match its siblings.

BUG FOUND BY VERIFYING (not by reading): the first pattern matched `dependencies = with python3Packages; [ ... ];` anywhere in flake.nix, so the NEW COMMENT explaining what the gate reads counted as a second declaration and the gate refused with "flake.nix has 2 blocks" on a good file. Anchored to `^[ \\t]*` so a line that has already opened a `#` cannot match. Regression test: tests/test_flake_deps_check.py::test_a_comment_quoting_the_block_is_not_a_second_block.

Measured: 0.07s, against ~2min for `nix flake check --print-build-logs`.
close_reason: scripts/flake_deps_check.py compares flake.nix's hand-mirrored dependency list against [project.dependencies], names each mismatch in both directions, runs in 0.07s as a pre-push hook and 'just flake-deps'; verified on constructed failures for dep-added-to-pyproject-only, dep-removed-from-flake-only, and the original flask defect

title: Pre-commit hook running seeds check, gating the mass-rewrite shape
description:
Wire `seeds check` into a git pre-commit hook.

## Why the git hook is the only durable gate

Claude Code's `PostToolUse` hooks fire on the Write/Edit *tools*. An agent using `bash -c 'cat > file'`, `sed -i`, or a Python one-liner never touches those tools and never fires the hook — and that is most agent file access in practice. So tool-level hooks are advisory, and **the git pre-commit hook is the only gate that holds, because everything reaches a commit eventually.**

@aguynamedryan, on making detection rather than prevention the strategy: *"we should check to see if metadata is being violated somehow and whatever other adherence we might want to enforce ... a check that's easily done."*

## Requirements

- Runs the violations tier; a violation blocks the commit.
- Runs `--against-git`, so a mass single-field rewrite demands explicit confirmation. This subsumes gating `D` and `R` in `git diff --name-status`, which matters because **there is no `delete` verb** (`db.delete_seed` has no callers outside its module) and without it `rm <seed-file>` becomes the de facto delete verb.
- Smells report but never block.
- Coexists with the pre-commit framework and the beads hooks. **`bd init` sets `core.hooksPath`, which the pre-commit framework refuses to install alongside.** The working wiring, its silent failure modes, and a reference implementation are in `~/.config/home-manager/docs/beads-git-hooks.md` — read it; do not reconstruct the procedure.

## Supersedes an older open seed

This closes what seeds-lcfa.1.1 asked for ("wire seeds sync into git hooks so the DB stops needing to be refreshed by hand") — but by removing the need rather than meeting it. After the cutover there is no sync to run, so the hook runs `check` instead. Note that as of 2026-08-31 that seed is still genuinely unshipped: `.pre-commit-config.yaml` has ruff, git-config-sanity, pytest and two beads hooks, and nothing for seeds.

## Accepted limitation

Pre-commit is detection *at commit*, not immutability. An agent can read corrupt state at any point before the commit fires. Not closable; it bounds damage to one working session rather than five weeks.

Source: seeds-sdhc, seeds-sdhc.2, seeds-lcfa.1.1, seeds-wurl
acceptance_criteria: A pre-commit hook runs the violations tier and --against-git; a violation or an unconfirmed mass single-field rewrite blocks the commit; smells do not block; the hook coexists with the pre-commit framework and the beads hooks per docs/beads-git-hooks.md.
notes:
Design picks (2-way, code-only, ruled per the overnight standing order):

1. ESCAPE HATCH = pre-commit's own SKIP, not a bespoke env var. The gate has to
   be confirmable — --against-git blocks a mass rewrite precisely because such a
   change needs a decision, not because it is forbidden. `SKIP=seeds-check git
   commit` is the framework mechanism, already understood, and it leaves every
   other hook running. A bespoke SEEDS_CHECK_ALLOW_* variable would have been a
   second mechanism for the same job. Rejected `git commit --no-verify` outright:
   it also skips the beads export and the git config sanity check.

2. THE STORE-MISSING CUE IS READ FROM THE FINDING, not from files_dir.is_dir().
   The hook asks check_violations and treats exactly one finding coded
   store-missing as "nothing to gate yet". Testing the directory directly would
   have been a second definition of "there is no store", free to drift from
   seeds.check's. Guarded by a test: one finding is the cue only when its code
   matches, so a store holding exactly one real violation still blocks.

3. PLACEMENT: commit stage, immediately after uv-lock-check and ahead of pytest.
   Pre-push is already ~79s and this is a per-commit data-integrity concern. It
   is not inserted above uv-lock-check, whose position is load-bearing.

Known consequence, documented in CONTRIBUTING.md and the config comment rather
than worked around: ONE intended mass rewrite needs SKIP TWICE. When the store
is unchanged relative to HEAD, check_against_git falls back to HEAD~1 vs HEAD
and audits the commit that just landed — the reading seeds-wurl needed, since
that sweep survived three days and three further commits. The next commit clears
it.
close_reason: scripts/seeds_check_hook.py wired as a commit-stage pre-commit hook: delegates to seeds check --against-git --smells, exits 0 when no seed-file store exists yet (reading the store-missing finding code, not a second predicate), blocks on violations and on the mass-rewrite shape including mass deletion; SKIP=seeds-check is the escape hatch

title: seeds history: structure the evolution from git, reading across the conversion
description:
Build `seeds history <id>` — render a seed's evolution from git, for a reader rather than for a diff tool.

## It structures and labels. It NEVER summarises.

Settled (seeds-sdhc.5). Summarising is the same editorial hazard the storage direction rejected on disk: a rolling summary of a deliberation is a decision log, which is what seeds exists not to be. Producing one on read adds a second defect — it is non-deterministic and unauditable, so two runs can disagree about what the journey was and neither is checkable.

This is seeds-152.5's cut applied cleanly: walking git and labelling changed fields is deterministic, so it is a verb; deciding what a change *meant* is judgment, so it belongs to the caller.

## It reads BOTH sides of the conversion

The problem this solves: writing 306 markdown files in one conversion commit gives every seed a one-entry history, orphaning ~113 commits of real deliberation on the day the format is supposed to make history better.

So: the seed's own file history back to the conversion commit, then the JSONL's history before it, joined into one list. The converter stamps `converted_at` so the reader knows where to switch.

**Rejected alternative:** replaying the JSONL history as synthetic per-file commits. That means ~113 fabricated commits appended to main in every repo that converts, and there is no honest way to do it that does not either rewrite history or lie about dates.

## Measured, so the shape is known

113 commits walked for one seed in **1.3 s**, producing exactly this:

    2026-08-25  Ryan Duryea   content,created_at,id,relationships   chore(seeds): capture seeds-lcfa — Dolt as s
    2026-08-26  Ryan Duryea   content,updated_at                    docs(seeds): correct the beads-has-no-Dolt-r
    2026-08-31  Ryan Duryea   content,title,updated_at              chore(seeds): attribute Ryan as @aguynamedry
    2026-08-31  Ryan Duryea   title,updated_at                      fix(seeds): restore the 83 titles clobbered

## Constraint to document loudly

**The JSONL stops being written, but its history stays load-bearing forever and must never be filtered out of git as cleanup.** The ruling that "the single JSONL is killed outright" is about the working tree, not about the past.

## Deferred, not settled

Granularity — per-commit versus per-section attribution via `git blame`. Per-commit is what the measurement implements and is enough to ship. Judge the refinement on the real thing after conversion.

Source: seeds-sdhc.5, seeds-bp0s, seeds-152.5, seeds-wurl
acceptance_criteria: 'seeds history <id>' lists per-commit date, author, changed fields and subject, and never emits prose summary; it joins the seed file's history back to converted_at with the pre-conversion JSONL history before it; a test asserts a seed created before conversion shows revisions from both sides.
notes:
Design picks (2-way, code-only, per the overnight ruling):
1. New module src/seeds/history.py for the join + field labelling, with the git PRIMITIVES (Commit, path_commits, show_file) added to the existing seeds.githistory. history.py shells out to nothing itself, so this is not a third git-walking implementation — githistory stays the single door to git, history.py stays the reader's view.
2. Output columns are exactly the four the acceptance criteria name — date, author, changed fields, subject — with no short-sha column. Auditability comes from the commit subject plus 'git log -- <path>', and adding a fifth column would have drifted from the measured shape the bead settled on.
Also: the conversion boundary is rendered as a '--- converted <ts> ---' divider between the two halves, and the two halves are ONE diff chain (each revision diffed against its predecessor regardless of source), so the conversion commit reports only what conversion changed rather than re-announcing every field.
close_reason: seeds history renders one line per commit in which the seed changed - date, author, changed fields, subject - never prose; the pre- and post-conversion halves are one diff chain bounded by converted_at, so the conversion commit reports only what conversion changed

title: seeds search over ripgrep; remove suggest and the FTS5 machinery
description:
Reimplement `seeds search` over ripgrep, and remove `seeds suggest` and the FTS5 machinery.

## Search

`seeds search` becomes a ripgrep pass with the status filter inline. Measured on the real corpus: `rg -l '<term>' $(rg --files-without-match '^status: abandoned' <dir>)` — **17 ms across 303 files**, one pass, no id bookkeeping.

## Removals

`Database.suggest` (db.py:1173), `sanitize_fts_query`, the `seeds_fts*` tables, and the `seeds suggest` command.

## The ruling, and the evidence behind it

@aguynamedryan, 2026-08-31: *"let's remove suggest/tend for now unless you have evidence we use suggest a lot."*

Evidence was gathered before agreeing: **roughly 15 genuine `suggest` invocations across 5 sessions** in the entire project transcript history, most agent-initiated during dedup passes rather than reached for by hand. Everything else matching is prose — docs, seed bodies, changelog, commit messages.

**Accepted casualty, stated so it is not treated as a bug later:** Porter stemming goes. ripgrep has no stemmer, so "merging" stops finding "merge". The offsetting measurement is that grep tested *broader* than FTS on a real query — 72 hits vs 77, and grep found one FTS missed ("contextual", which Porter has no `-ual` rule for). What SQLite uniquely provided was ranking, not recall.

seeds-lcfa.6.1 existed to force this answer before anything was deleted, and is resolved.

Source: seeds-lcfa.6.1, seeds-142.1, seeds-fkb8, seeds-ebg1
acceptance_criteria: 'seeds search' returns matches via ripgrep with the status filter inline; Database.suggest, sanitize_fts_query, the seeds_fts* tables and the 'seeds suggest' command are gone; 'seeds --help' does not list suggest.
notes:
Design picks (2-way, code-only, per the overnight ruling):
1. The search query is passed to ripgrep as a REGEX (rg's default), case-insensitively, not as a fixed string. Regex is strictly more capable, hyphens and quotes are already literal in it, and a malformed pattern now RAISES (StoreError naming rg's own message) rather than silently returning nothing.
2. The status filter is the measured two-stage form: 'rg --files-without-match ^status: (resolved|abandoned)$' over the directory, then the query over exactly those paths. When the candidate set is empty the second rg is skipped entirely -- rg with no path arguments searches the working directory, which would answer a question nobody asked with hits from source files that are not seeds.
3. ripgrep is declared in flake.nix as a real runtime dependency (makeWrapper --prefix PATH) as well as in nativeCheckInputs. Without the wrap, 'nix run . -- search' works only where rg happens to be installed. Verified with 'env -i'. The Python-side StoreError naming ripgrep stays for the pip/uv-tool routes that cannot wrap anything; CI asserts 'rg --version' before pytest.
4. Search results are id-sorted. FTS ordered by BM25 rank and ripgrep has no ranking to offer, so a deterministic order beats directory order (which makes two runs of the same command disagree).
close_reason: seeds search is a two-stage ripgrep pass with the status filter inline; suggest, sanitize_fts_query, tokenize_for_suggest, ScoredSeed and the seeds_fts tables are gone; ripgrep declared in flake.nix and asserted in CI, after the nix sandbox caught its absence

## Why now
