title: seeds migrate-ids converts base36 hash IDs to sequential — reverses the current ID scheme
description:
`seeds migrate-ids` migrates hash IDs -> sequential IDs. That was correct when sequential was the target scheme. It is now backwards: seeds-199 established **base36 hash IDs as the standard going forward** (shipped via seeds-tek + seeds-mlj), with sequential grandfathered as legacy.

Running the command today silently destroys the current scheme.

Found during a follow-up audit after seeds-skc, sweeping for other numeric-only ID assumptions.

## Reproduced (temp database, not the real one)

```
$ seeds jot alpha / beta / gamma
seeds-a5h, seeds-aiy, seeds-e1l          # base36 hash — the current scheme

$ seeds migrate-ids
Migrated 3 seeds to sequential IDs:
  seeds-a5h → seeds-1
  seeds-aiy → seeds-2
  seeds-e1l → seeds-3
```

## Why it fires

`Database.migrate_to_sequential_ids` (src/seeds/db.py:~900) decides whether migration is needed with:

```python
if parse_sequential_id(sid) is None:
    has_hex_ids = True
```

`parse_sequential_id` returns None for anything non-numeric — which, by design, includes every base36 hash ID. So a fully-modern database reads as "full of un-migrated hex IDs" and gets renumbered.

The CLI command (src/seeds/cli.py:1292) has **no guard and no confirmation prompt**. It does write a `.db.bak` first, so it is recoverable — but it also re-exports `seeds.jsonl`, so the damage lands in the git-tracked file and would be committed by the normal hooks.

## The hard part, if you try to guard rather than remove

Distinguishing "legacy hex hash" from "modern base36 hash" by shape is not reliably possible: hex `[0-9a-f]` is a strict SUBSET of base36 `[0-9a-z]`. `seeds-a5h` is unambiguously base36 (contains 'h'), but `seeds-abc` is valid as both. Same irreducible shape-ambiguity documented in seeds-6hj5.

## Options

- **(a) Remove the command.** Cleanest. It was a one-time migration for a transition that has concluded, and it now only does harm. Anyone with a genuinely ancient hex database can pin an old release.
- **(b) Hard-deprecate.** Keep the command but make it exit non-zero with an explanation pointing at seeds-199. Preserves discoverability for anyone who remembers it existed.
- **(c) Guard on shape.** Not recommended — unreliable per the hex-subset-of-base36 problem above, and it would still be a command whose purpose is obsolete.

Recommendation: **(a)**, falling back to **(b)** if removing a shipped CLI command feels too abrupt for a pre-1.0 tool. Needs Ryan's call, since it removes user-facing surface.

Note `bd`-side naming: the sibling concern about validation is seed seeds-6hj5, not a bead.
acceptance_criteria:
- On a database of base36 hash IDs, `seeds migrate-ids` either no longer exists (option a) or exits non-zero without mutating anything (option b).
- Verified concretely: create 3 seeds via `seeds jot` in a temp SEEDS_DIR, record their IDs, run the command, confirm the IDs are unchanged (option b) or the command is absent from `seeds --help` (option a).
- `seeds --help` no longer advertises migrating to sequential IDs as a normal workflow.
- No .db.bak is left behind by a run that changes nothing.
- Full suite green: `uv run pytest`. Any tests covering migrate_to_sequential_ids are removed or updated to match the chosen option rather than deleted silently.
notes: RULING FROM RYAN (2026-07-27): option (a) — HARD REMOVE, no deprecation shim. "We're definitely not going to be able to do that going forward, and this is not a feature we need to support anymore... I don't know that anyone else is using anything, so we'll just hard remove." Safety audit confirmed: no docs, no prime.py text, no __init__ exports, no callers outside the migration itself. parse_sequential_id's only src caller is the migration, so it goes too — suffix.isdigit() already covers legacy-ID detection where needed.
close_reason: hard-removed migrate-ids CLI command, Database.migrate_to_sequential_ids, and parse_sequential_id (281 lines). Severity was higher than first written up: the migration renumbered the ENTIRE database from 1 whenever even a single non-sequential ID was present, so running it on the real 267-seed db (265 grandfathered + 2 base36) would have renumbered all of them, not just the 2.

title: flake.nix declares x86_64-darwin, which nixpkgs 26.11 dropped
description:
`flake.nix` lists `x86_64-darwin` in its `systems` array (lines 8-13), but nixpkgs-unstable has rolled to 26.11, which **removed x86_64-darwin entirely**. The flake therefore advertises a platform it cannot evaluate, let alone build.

Found while implementing seeds-80g. Independently reproduced on titan.

## Reproduction

```
$ nix flake check --all-systems
checking derivation packages.x86_64-linux.default...   ok
checking derivation packages.aarch64-linux.default...  ok
checking derivation packages.x86_64-darwin.default...
error: Nixpkgs 26.11 has dropped support for x86_64-darwin.
   ... suggests url = "github:NixOS/nixpkgs/nixpkgs-26.05-darwin";
   See https://nixos.org/manual/nixpkgs/unstable/release-notes#x86_64-darwin-26.11
```

Note it fails at **evaluation**, not build — so no builder/emulation setup can work around it.

## Impact

1. **Public Intel-Mac users** hitting `nix run github:outcomesinsights/seeds` get a hard failure. This is the exact "broken promise in the README" that seeds-80g exists to prevent, and CI does not currently catch it (see below).
2. `nix flake check` hard-fails on ANY darwin machine, and `--all-systems` fails everywhere.
3. **CI is blind to it.** seeds-80g deliberately ships a bare native-only `nix flake check` precisely BECAUSE `--all-systems` fails on this. Fixing this bug is what would let CI check the full matrix.

Does NOT affect Ryan's own hosts: home-manager `flake.nix` declares `aarch64-darwin` for all three darwin hosts (lines 163, 170, 179) and `x86_64-linux` for titan. No x86_64-darwin anywhere. So this is a public-facing defect, not a local one — which is why it's P2 and not P1.

## Two-way decision (pick ONE, don't invent a third)

- **(a) Drop `x86_64-darwin` from the `systems` list.** Simple, one line, matches nixpkgs reality. Cost: Intel Macs lose the nix install path entirely (they can still `uv tool install`).
- **(b) Pin a separate nixpkgs input (`nixpkgs-26.05-darwin`) for that one system.** Keeps Intel Mac support. Cost: a second nixpkgs input, per-system nixpkgs selection logic, and an input frozen on a release branch that will itself age out.

Recommendation: **(a)**. Declaring a platform you cannot build is worse than not declaring it, and Intel Macs are EOL upstream. But this changes the systems list set in seeds-0y4, so it's a deliberate reversal, not a silent tweak — record the rationale.

## Follow-on

If (a) is chosen, seeds-80g's CI job can be upgraded from bare `nix flake check` to `nix flake check --all-systems` in the same change, since the blocker is gone. Verify that actually passes on an x86_64-linux runner before claiming it — the remaining foreign systems (aarch64-linux, aarch64-darwin) may still fail to *build* even if they evaluate.
acceptance_criteria:
- `nix flake check --all-systems` exits 0 on titan (x86_64-linux), OR the CI job is explicitly documented as native-only with the reason recorded in flake.nix.
- If option (a): `grep -q 'x86_64-darwin' flake.nix` returns no match.
- If option (b): `jq -e '.nodes | keys' flake.lock` shows the second darwin nixpkgs input, and `nix eval .#packages.x86_64-darwin.default.version` exits 0.
- `nix build .#default` still exits 0 and `nix run . -- --version` still prints `seeds, version 0.3.5` (no regression on the native path).
- The chosen option and its rationale are recorded as a comment in flake.nix.
notes:
RULING FROM RYAN (2026-07-26): **Option (a) — drop `x86_64-darwin`.** Do not implement option (b); do not pin a second nixpkgs input. This is a deliberate reversal of the systems list set in seeds-0y4 — record the reason in a flake.nix comment so a future reader doesn't "restore" the missing platform.

Follow-on is now IN SCOPE for this bead: once x86_64-darwin is gone, try upgrading seeds-80g's CI job from bare `nix flake check` to `nix flake check --all-systems`. Verify it actually passes on x86_64-linux before claiming it — aarch64-linux and aarch64-darwin may still fail to BUILD even though they now evaluate. If --all-systems does not pass cleanly, leave the CI job native-only and say so plainly in the report rather than forcing it.
close_reason: dropped x86_64-darwin (nixpkgs 26.11 removed it); CI upgraded to nix flake check --all-systems

title: Add nix build job to CI so the flake can't silently rot
description:
Add a job to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` that builds the flake on every push/PR to main.

Source: seeds-gf69. Depends on seeds-0y4 (the flake must exist first).

## Motivation

This is a hard prerequisite of shipping the flake, not a nice-to-have. From the deliberation: **a flake that silently rots is worse than no flake — it becomes a broken promise in the README.** Once `nix run github:outcomesinsights/seeds` is documented, it has to keep working, and nothing else in CI exercises the nix path.

It also catches the one recurring maintenance wrinkle automatically: when a declared dependency floor in `pyproject.toml` outruns what nixpkgs-unstable ships (today `flask>=3.1.3` vs nixpkgs' 3.1.2, handled by `pythonRelaxDeps`), the nix build is the only thing that notices.

## Constraints

- Use `DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action` (or `cachix/install-nix-action`) — pick one, don't hand-roll a nix install.
- Run `nix flake check`, which covers both the build and the pytest suite via `checks.default`. A bare `nix build` would skip the tests, since the locked design deliberately keeps `doCheck` off `packages.default`.
- Keep it a separate job from `lint` and `test` so a nix-side failure is legible at a glance.
- `ubuntu-latest` only. Do NOT add a macOS runner — this repo is private-billed and the deliberation explicitly deprioritized breadth here.

## Existing ci.yml shape (for reference)

Two jobs today: `lint` (ruff check, ruff format --check, mypy) and `test` (pytest across Python 3.10–3.13). Both use `actions/checkout@v7` + `astral-sh/setup-uv@v7`.

Suggested job to append:

```yaml
  nix:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action@main
      - run: nix flake check --print-build-logs
      - run: nix run . -- --version
```
acceptance_criteria:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` contains a job named `nix`.
- `yq '.jobs.nix.runs-on' .github/workflows/ci.yml` outputs `ubuntu-latest`.
- The job's steps include a `nix flake check` invocation (`grep -q 'nix flake check' .github/workflows/ci.yml`).
- `yq '.jobs | keys' .github/workflows/ci.yml` still lists `lint` and `test` (existing jobs untouched).
- The workflow file is valid YAML: `yq '.' .github/workflows/ci.yml > /dev/null` exits 0.
notes:
Discovered while implementing seeds-0y4 (verified independently on main):

- `nix flake check` on Nix 2.24 only checks the CURRENT system by default. Observed output: "warning: The check omitted these incompatible systems: aarch64-darwin, aarch64-linux, x86_64-darwin. Use '--all-systems' to check all."
  The suggested YAML in this bead's description uses a bare `nix flake check`, which therefore validates x86_64-linux only.
  TENSION TO RESOLVE (don't assume `--all-systems` is right): on a single ubuntu-latest runner, `--all-systems` will evaluate the foreign-system derivations but cannot build them without emulation or remote builders. Decide deliberately whether the CI job should (a) stay native-only and accept x86_64-linux coverage, or (b) add `--all-systems` for evaluation-level coverage of the other three. If (b) turns out to fail the job, fall back to (a) — do NOT add QEMU or remote builders, that's scope creep.
- The flake resolves to python 3.14.6; suite green there (433 passed).
- nixpkgs-unstable now ships flask 3.1.3, so `pythonRelaxDeps = [ "flask" ]` is currently a no-op. It was kept deliberately per the locked decision in seeds-0y4 — leave it alone.
DECISION (seeds-80g impl): the nix CI job runs a BARE `nix flake check --print-build-logs` — option (a), native x86_64-linux only. NOT --all-systems.

Tested by hand in the repo before deciding, not assumed:
  $ nix flake check --all-systems --print-build-logs   ->  EXIT 1
  checking derivation packages.x86_64-linux.default...   ok
  checking derivation packages.aarch64-linux.default...  ok
  checking derivation packages.x86_64-darwin.default...
  error: Nixpkgs 26.11 has dropped support for x86_64-darwin.

Key nuance vs. what the bead anticipated: --all-systems does not fail for the
predicted reason (no emulation / remote builder to BUILD foreign systems). It
fails earlier, at EVALUATION, because nixpkgs-unstable is now 26.11 and 26.11
removed x86_64-darwin entirely — a system flake.nix still declares. So no
builder setup could rescue option (b); the only fixes would be dropping
x86_64-darwin from the flake systems list or pinning nixpkgs to a 26.05-darwin
branch. Both are changes to the seeds-0y4 locked flake design, out of scope
here. Falling back to (a) per this bead`s own instruction.

  $ nix flake check --print-build-logs   ->  EXIT 0  (433 passed in 13.73s, py 3.14.6)
  $ nix run . -- --version               ->  EXIT 0  "seeds, version 0.3.5"

Installer action: DeterminateSystems/nix-installer-action@main, per the bead
suggestion and that action`s own documented usage. Verified from its README
that it writes nix-command + flakes into nix.conf by default, so the job does
NOT pass --extra-experimental-features (needed only for hand-runs on this box).
Residual nit, not acted on: @main is a moving ref that the repo`s
github-actions Dependabot config cannot bump, unlike the @v7 pins on
actions/checkout and astral-sh/setup-uv.
close_reason: nix job added to ci.yml running native nix flake check + nix run smoke test

title: Author the `promote` distillation skill (SKILL.md)
description:
Author the `promote` distillation skill — the judgment half of the lodestone output mode. A thin prompt-macro that distills a matured seed into one bounded principle and calls `seeds promote`. Ships in the seeds Claude Code plugin.

NOTE ON IDS: "Source" IDs below are seeds-TOOL ids (numeric/dotted, e.g. seeds-147.1). Read them with `seeds show <id>` — they are NOT bead ids.

## Why (motivation)
The `seeds promote` verb (see the verb bead) does deterministic bookkeeping but cannot decide WHAT one line to write or WHICH file it belongs in — that is language judgment. Per the seeds-152.5 cut, that judgment lives in a thin skill, auto-discovered by its `description` when a user wants to promote a matured deliberation.

## Locked decisions (constraints)
- Phrasing discipline is the load-bearing constraint (seeds-147.1). The distilled principle MUST be bounded and scoped, never an open-ended imperative. This is the whole reason the step needs a model's judgment. The skill must quote BOTH the good and the bad shape (verbatim, in the content below).
- The skill ADVISES the target file; the user decides. Agent directive -> CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md; domain pillar -> README. NO ADR path (the stakeholder does not use ADRs).
- User-initiated, run once. Match the closing line of the sibling skills.
- Skills are auto-discovered from the skills/ directory — NO edit to plugin.json or marketplace.json is required.

## File to create (VERBATIM content)
Create `src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/skills/promote/SKILL.md` containing exactly:

---
name: promote
description: Use when a deliberation captured in seeds has matured into a load-bearing principle the user wants promoted into durable, always-on project context (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / README) — distills the seed into one crisp bounded line and calls `seeds promote`.
---

# Promote a seed to a lodestone

The user has a seed whose deliberation has settled into a load-bearing principle — a "lodestone" — that future work in this project should be steered by. A lodestone is not a new kind of seed; it is an ordinary seed that gets **resolved** with its decision **distilled into one crisp line and promoted into durable project context**. The always-in-front-of-the-agent job is handled by the runtime injecting that file every session — not by anything seeds surfaces internally.

Promote once, when invoked. Do not adopt this as default behavior for later turns.

## Steps

1. **Absorb the deliberation.** `seeds show <id>` and walk its thread (parents, children, related) so the principle you write reflects the whole reasoning, not just the title.

2. **Distill to ONE crisp, bounded principle.** This is the load-bearing judgment and the reason this is a skill, not just a command. The principle must be *bounded and scoped*, never an open-ended imperative:
   - GOOD (bounded, scoped): "a code set has exactly one vocabulary ID."
   - BAD (open-ended, detonates): "respect deprecations and move forward."

   Why it matters: promoted principles land in always-on agent context and are read as hard rules. An open-ended imperative once led an agent to strip 33 function instances across a codebase during a routine upgrade because a changelog gave off "deprecated vibes" — the principle had become a trigger. Promotion is *distillation into one weighted line*, not a copy-paste of the deliberation. Propose the line and get the user's confirmation before writing.

3. **Advise the target file.** Where durable context lives:
   - Agent-behavior directive -> `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md`.
   - Domain / product pillar -> `README` (or wherever the project keeps durable prose).

   Propose the target; let the user override.

4. **Promote.** Run:

       seeds promote <id> --to <file> --as "<the one-line principle>"

   This appends a provenance-stamped bullet to the file, records the back-link on the seed (resolution text + a `lodestone` tag), and resolves the seed. Pass `--no-resolve` only if the user wants to keep deliberating.

5. **Confirm both ends of the two-way link landed** — the bullet in `<file>` cites the seed ID; the resolved seed's resolution names the file.

(END OF VERBATIM SKILL.md CONTENT — the frontmatter delimiters `---` above and below the name/description block are part of the file.)

## Acceptance
- `src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/skills/promote/SKILL.md` exists, opening with YAML frontmatter containing `name: promote` and a `description:` line.
- The body contains BOTH the good example ("a code set has exactly one vocabulary ID") and the bad example ("respect deprecations and move forward").
- The body instructs calling `seeds promote <id> --to <file> --as`.
- `uv run pytest` still green (no code changed; confirm nothing broke).

Source: seeds-147.4 (build spec), seeds-147.3 (decisions), seeds-147.1 (phrasing discipline / the Jigsaw 33-refactor cautionary tale), seeds-152.4 + seeds-187 (sibling skills whose tone to mirror).
notes: DECISION (seeds-197, 2026-07-15): prime will NOT advertise this skill, so the skill's own keyword-triggering is the PRIMARY agent-facing discovery path — make it robust. The `description:` frontmatter MUST auto-trigger on BOTH keywords 'promote' AND 'lodestone'. Ensure both words appear, e.g.: 'Use when the user wants to promote a seed to a lodestone — a load-bearing principle distilled into durable, always-on project context (CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md / README) ...'. Keep the rest of the SKILL.md body as specified in the description.

title: Single-source the package version to stop drift across 4 files
description:
The version string must currently be hand-edited in FOUR places, which already drifted in practice: the two plugin manifests sat at 0.2.0 while the CLI was 0.3.1, contributing to stale/disabled plugin installs (the seeds:* skills not loading). Establish a single source of truth and a guard so the four can never silently diverge again.

The four places:
1. pyproject.toml -> [project].version
2. src/seeds/__init__.py -> __version__
3. src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json -> version
4. src/seeds/plugin/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json -> plugins[0].version
design:
Canonical source = src/seeds/__init__.py __version__.
- pyproject.toml: drop the hardcoded version; use hatchling dynamic version ([project].dynamic=['version'] + [tool.hatch.version].path='src/seeds/__init__.py'). pyproject is then DERIVED and can never be wrong.
- The two plugin JSON manifests must hold a literal version (Claude Code reads them as static files; they cannot be runtime-dynamic). Provide one command to update them: scripts/bump_version.py VERSION (wrapped by 'just bump-version VERSION') rewrites __init__.py + both JSON manifests. pyproject auto-derives.
- Guard against drift with a test asserting plugin.json and marketplace.json version == seeds.__version__, so any future divergence fails pre-commit/CI.
acceptance_criteria:
- pyproject.toml has no hardcoded version literal (uses dynamic + tool.hatch.version).
- uv build produces seeds-<__version__>-*.whl matching src/seeds/__init__.py.
- 'just bump-version X.Y.Z' updates __init__.py, plugin.json, and marketplace.json together.
- A pytest test fails when any plugin manifest version != seeds.__version__.
- uv run pytest passes.
close_reason: Implemented: pyproject derives version from src/seeds/__init__.py (hatchling dynamic); scripts/bump_version.py + just bump-version sync the two plugin manifests; tests/test_version_sync.py guards against drift. Committed in 578f738.

title: Add 'seeds skills install' CLI command and update pyproject.toml package data
description:
Implement the CLI entry point that registers the bundled marketplace with Claude Code and installs the seeds plugin. Make it idempotent so re-running after `uv tool upgrade seeds` picks up updated skill content.

Reference deliberation: seeds-152.3 (decision to ship as plugin), seeds-154 answer (commands and Python skeleton).

## Implementation outline (src/seeds/cli.py)

Add a `skills` Click group with an `install` subcommand:

```python
import importlib.resources
import shutil
import subprocess
import click

@cli.group()
def skills() -> None:
    """Manage Claude Code skills shipped with seeds."""

@skills.command()
def install() -> None:
    """Install the seeds Claude Code plugin (provides seeds:* skills)."""
    if not shutil.which("claude"):
        click.echo("`claude` CLI not found. Install Claude Code first.", err=True)
        raise click.Abort()

    plugin_root = importlib.resources.files("seeds") / "plugin"
    plugin_path = str(plugin_root)

    # Register the local marketplace (idempotent — re-adding is a no-op or warning)
    subprocess.run(
        ["claude", "plugin", "marketplace", "add", plugin_path],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=False,
    )

    # Detect whether plugin is already installed, choose install vs update
    list_result = subprocess.run(
        ["claude", "plugin", "list"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=False,
    )
    action = "update" if "seeds@seeds-marketplace" in list_result.stdout else "install"

    result = subprocess.run(
        ["claude", "plugin", action, "seeds@seeds-marketplace", "--scope", "user"],
        capture_output=True, text=True, check=False,
    )
    if result.returncode != 0:
        click.echo(f"Plugin {action} failed: {result.stderr}", err=True)
        raise click.Abort()

    click.echo(f"seeds plugin {action}ed successfully")
```

Adjust style/imports to match the existing cli.py conventions (the project already imports click and uses Click groups — follow the existing pattern).

## pyproject.toml update

Hatchling auto-includes non-Python files under packages directories but may exclude dot-prefixed directories (like .claude-plugin/). Add explicit inclusion to be safe:

```toml
[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel]
packages = ["src/seeds"]

[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]
"src/seeds/plugin" = "seeds/plugin"
```

(Add the `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]` section after the existing wheel target section.)

## Style

- Use type hints to match existing cli.py (already uses `from __future__ import annotations` and `-> None`).
- Keep messages terse.
- Don't add tests in this bead — the e2e verification bead handles that.
acceptance_criteria:
1. `seeds skills --help` runs and shows the install subcommand
2. `seeds skills install --help` runs and shows usage
3. `seeds skills install` exits 0 on a system with `claude` CLI present (assume it is present for this bead)
4. Implementation locates the plugin path via importlib.resources (NOT a hardcoded absolute path)
5. Implementation calls `claude plugin marketplace add`, then either `claude plugin install` or `claude plugin update` based on whether the plugin is already in `claude plugin list` output
6. Graceful error if `claude` CLI is missing: clear message to stderr, non-zero exit
7. pyproject.toml has `[tool.hatch.build.targets.wheel.force-include]` mapping `src/seeds/plugin` to `seeds/plugin`
8. Running `uv build` produces a wheel that contains the plugin tree (verifiable with `unzip -l dist/seeds-*.whl | grep plugin`)
9. Existing tests still pass: `uv run pytest`
close_reason: Added seeds skills install CLI command + force-include in pyproject

title: End-to-end test the feedback skill install
description:
Verify the full install flow works against the locally-installed seeds CLI. This is the spike's success criterion: the user can run one command and have the seeds:feedback skill available in Claude Code.

Reference: seeds-152.3 (install path), seeds-154 (mechanism).

## Verification steps

1. Clean reinstall the global seeds CLI:
   ```bash
   uv cache clean seeds
   uv tool uninstall seeds
   uv tool install --reinstall .
   ```

2. Run the new install command:
   ```bash
   seeds skills install
   ```

3. Verify plugin is registered:
   ```bash
   claude plugin list | grep 'seeds@seeds-marketplace'
   ```

4. Verify marketplace is registered:
   ```bash
   claude plugin marketplace list | grep seeds-marketplace
   ```

5. Inspect the install cache for the SKILL.md:
   ```bash
   find ~/.claude/plugins/cache -path '*seeds-marketplace*' -name 'SKILL.md'
   ```

6. Idempotency check — re-run install, should succeed without error:
   ```bash
   seeds skills install
   ```
   Should produce "seeds plugin updated successfully" (or similar) on the second run, confirming the install→update branch works.

7. Document any issues encountered and any fixes applied to other beads or pyproject.toml in the bead notes.

- Don't push to remote.
- Don't modify the project's .seeds/ database.
- Don't write fancy automated tests — this is a manual verification step. The deliverable is the verification log.
- Don't worry about other Claude Code sessions picking up the skill in real-time; that takes a session restart.

title: Write feedback SKILL.md content for the seeds Claude Code plugin
description:
Write the feedback skill — a prompt macro shipped via the seeds Claude Code plugin. When invoked, it frames the next user utterance as feedback on the agent's prior turn and instructs the agent to invite further questions/comments/criticisms exactly once.

Reference deliberation:

```markdown
---
name: feedback
description: Use when the user signals they are providing feedback on your prior turn, or asks you to treat their next message as feedback. Sets up a single-turn dynamic where you incorporate the feedback and invite further pushback.
---

# Feedback turn

Treat the following user message as feedback, corrections, or observations on your previous reply — not as a new instruction.

After incorporating the feedback, invite the user to provide further questions, comments, or criticisms to continue refining the discussion. Do this once, for this reply only. Do not adopt this closing invitation as a default for subsequent turns — its value comes from being user-initiated.
```

description:
## Why
Local pre-commit runs ruff and pytest but skips mypy. mypy is part of CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml lint job), so type errors slip past commit time and only surface on push. Adding mypy as a local pre-commit step would catch them at the same moment as the other lints.

title: Validate seed-ID cross-references on create/update
description:
## Why

Claude has hallucinated seed-ID cross-references in newly-written bodies multiple times (CSC 4/23, oimnibus 5/8). When it doesn't self-catch, the graph silently degrades.

Source: seeds-142.3.

## What

On `seeds create` / `seeds update` (including `--append`), scan title + content + resolution for `<prefix>-NNN[.NNN]*` patterns. For each match, verify the seed exists. If any don't:
- Default: hard fail with a clear error listing the unknown IDs
- `--allow-unknown-refs` flag to override (for legitimate forward-references during multi-step builds)

## Open design questions (decide during implementation)
- Default fail vs default warn?
- Tolerant of `seed-87` (singular) vs strict `seeds-87` only?

## Acceptance
- `seeds create -t '...' -c 'see seeds-99999'` (nonexistent) fails with a clear error
- Same content with `--allow-unknown-refs` succeeds
- `seeds update <id> --append 'see seeds-99999'` fails identically
- A reference to an existing seed (e.g. `seeds-2`) succeeds normally
- A reference to a child ID (e.g. `seeds-142.1`) is validated correctly
close_reason: Implemented validation in create/update with --allow-unknown-refs override. 11 pytest cases cover unknown/existing/child refs in title/content/append, plus the override flag.

title: seeds sync: guard against flushing into commits with unrelated staged code
description: The pre-commit invocation of `seeds sync --flush-only` rewrites `.seeds/seeds.jsonl` from current `seeds.db` state and lets the pre-commit framework re-stage the file. Any pending seed.db changes therefore get baked into whatever commit fires next, regardless of topic. Surfaced in code_set_catalog: commit 49c466f (csc-kur, vocab-chip feature) absorbed 46 lines of unrelated seed-resolution diffs (~23 prior resolutions). Author-discipline workaround is fragile and known to fail under cognitive load. Need a structural guard at the seeds CLI layer so every consuming project benefits without per-repo bandaids.
design:
Two options; pick one before implementation.

**Option A — refuse (recommended).**
Exit non-zero with a two-line message:
  'seeds: refusing to flush — the export would modify .seeds/seeds.jsonl but staged code is unrelated.'
  'Resolve with EITHER \`git commit\` the code first then re-run, OR \`git stash --keep-index\` and create a dedicated \`chore(seeds): …\` commit.'
Authors keep full control; the hook never silently mixes topics.

**Option B — warn.**
Print a clearly-formatted warning to stderr and proceed. Lower friction; lower assurance. Pre-commit output is noisy and warnings get missed — downside is real.

Detection logic (either option):
- \`git diff --cached --name-only -- ':!.seeds/'\` lists staged paths outside .seeds/.
- Compare seeds.db state against current seeds.jsonl to know whether flush would actually change anything.
- Skip the guard entirely if not inside a git working tree (\`seeds sync\` is also called outside hook contexts).

Surface choice:
- **Always-on (default behavior change).** Cleanest, but breaks workflows that intentionally bundle seed + code in one commit. Probably acceptable since intentional-bundling is rare and explicit override is easy.
- **Flag-gated.** New flag like \`--guard-mixed-stage\` (or a \`seeds hooks pre-commit\` subcommand that's the recommended hook entry). Backward-compatible but requires every project to update its pre-commit config.

Recommendation: always-on with an opt-out flag (\`--allow-mixed-stage\`) for the rare intentional case, plus the message in Option A pointing to the two clean alternatives. That puts the right default in place without locking out legitimate exceptions.

Edge cases:
- Initial commit (no HEAD): \`git diff --cached\` still works; treat as if nothing in HEAD.
- Pre-commit framework's --all-files mode: same logic applies; guard just fires on whatever is staged.
- Author runs \`seeds sync\` outside a hook (e.g., manual flush before \`git add\`): not in commit context, skip guard.
acceptance_criteria:
- The pre-commit invocation of seeds sync detects the contamination scenario:
  (a) running the flush would actually change .seeds/seeds.jsonl (db has unflushed deltas), AND
  (b) git diff --cached --name-only -- ':!.seeds/' is non-empty (staged code outside .seeds/).
- In that scenario, the command refuses or warns per the chosen design (see Design).
- Seed-only commits (clean code tree, only seed changes staged) flow normally with no friction.
- No-op syncs (no pending db deltas) flow normally regardless of what else is staged.
- Behavior degrades gracefully outside a git working tree — guard only fires when git is present and a commit context can be inferred.
- Test coverage exercises: contamination case, seed-only case, no-op case, no-git case.
- Behavior change is visible in --help and CHANGELOG; downstream projects know what to expect.
notes:
Origin: surfaced in code_set_catalog (~/projects/outins/code_set_catalog). Downstream tracker bead csc-87g in that workspace is being closed and pointed at this bead. No downstream tracker is being filed — once this ships, code_set_catalog (and other consumers) bump the seeds version and adopt naturally. Verification of the contamination case can happen against this bead's own test suite; doesn't need a separate per-project verification task.

Memory note in code_set_catalog beads: \`resolve-seeds-in-their-own-dedicated-session-never\` (the workaround that this bead obsoletes).

Per-commit-message convention: when the guard fires in code_set_catalog, the suggested rescue is \`chore(seeds): resolve N settled seeds\` as a dedicated commit.

--- DESIGN RULED (Ryan, 2026-08-26) ---

Option A, always-on, with `--allow-mixed-stage` as the opt-out. This is the bead's own recommendation, chosen over warn-and-proceed and over flag-gating.

Reasoning, load-bearing and not to be re-opened: warn-and-proceed loses to the bead's own observation that pre-commit output is noisy and warnings get missed -- which is the exact failure being fixed. Flag-gating protects nobody by default, since every consuming repo would have to update its pre-commit config before the guard does anything.

Exact message text approved:

  seeds: refusing to flush -- the export would modify .seeds/seeds.jsonl but staged code is unrelated.
  Resolve with EITHER `git commit` the code first then re-run, OR `git stash --keep-index` and create a dedicated `chore(seeds): ...` commit.

Mention the `--allow-mixed-stage` override in the refusal output so the escape hatch is discoverable at the moment it is needed.

BREAKING: this is a default-behaviour change and the THIRD in v0.6.0. Commit it with a `!` in the subject and a `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer -- the other two fixes in this release needed that added after the fact, so do it at authoring time here.

INTERACTION worth knowing (seed seeds-lcfa.1.1, not yet built): there is an open proposal to wire `seeds sync` into post-merge/post-checkout/pre-commit hooks so the DB stops needing manual refresh. If that lands, this guard fires considerably more often, because a flush would then be attempted on every commit rather than only where a project wired it up. That is an argument for getting the refusal message right, not an argument against the guard.
close_reason: seeds sync refuses to flush when the export would change seeds.jsonl while unrelated code is staged; --allow-mixed-stage overrides

title: Seed IDs adopt a tilde separator so they can never be confused with bead IDs
description:
Ruled by @aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01: "if beads/seeds ids are so easily confused, perhaps we should change seeds IDs (again) to be recognizably different from beads? this would probably help me as a user as well".

THE COLLISION IS SYSTEMIC, not a quirk of this repo. Both tools derive their prefix from the project name, so they are IDENTICAL in every repo measured: seeds=seeds/beads=seeds here, pman/pman, csc/csc. And the shapes match too - bead seeds-4co.19 against seed seeds-lcfa.6.1 share prefix, base36 hash and dotted children. Nothing distinguishes them.

SEPARATOR: tilde, chosen over underscore and equals. It is literal in regex, so the cross-repo rg recipe documented in prime keeps working unescaped; legal on every filesystem including Windows; safe unquoted in shell; carries no other meaning in the corpus. Rejected: "+" is a regex quantifier and would break rg; "@" collides with the @handles used throughout seed bodies; ":" is illegal on Windows; "_" is too close to "-" to do the one job this exists for.

    bead:  seeds-4co.19
    seed:  seeds~sdhc.6.1

SCOPE - the grammar change reaches further than the storage change did:
- the id regex (docs/storage-format.md currently ^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*-[0-9a-z]+(\.[0-9]+)*$)
- seedfile.path_for_id / id_for_path, and the filename rule
- the ref validator, incl. its base36-hash detection
- rename-prefix, whose NEW_PREFIX validator today allows only lowercase, digits and hyphens
- convert, which must emit tilde ids directly so a pre-0.7 store converts once into the final shape
- prime, README, docs/storage-format.md, working-with-seeds.md

MEASURED MIGRATION COST on this repo: 1,996 seed-id references inside seed bodies (rename-prefix rewrites these), 309 files to rename, 45 seed ids cited in bead descriptions (NOT rewritten - they go stale and need a sweep), and 759 in commit messages (permanently stale; history is immutable and that is accepted).

SEQUENCING, and it matters: do this BEFORE the other 14 repos convert. They convert on demand as @aguynamedryan reaches for seeds in each one, so every repo that converts before this lands converts twice. Right now only this repo has converted, which makes now the cheapest this will ever be.

Source: seeds-32ai (which asked whether ids should be topic slugs), seeds-4co.9
acceptance_criteria: A seed id is <prefix>~<hash>[.N...] and its file is .seeds/seeds/<prefix>~<hash>.md. The reader, writer, id/path mapping, ref validator, rename-prefix, converter and docs all use the new grammar. Converting a pre-0.7 store produces tilde ids directly. This repo migrates: 309 files renamed and all 1996 in-body references rewritten, seeds check clean afterwards, and seeds history still renders across the conversion for a seed that existed before it. rg 'seeds~sdhc' matches literally.
notes:
STOPPED MID-FLIGHT and deferred (@aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01). The agent was killed a few minutes in, having written nothing outside its worktree; the live store was untouched — 309 files, zero tilde ids. Do NOT pick this up until the ID scheme is settled as a whole.

Why it was stopped, and the arguments are ones I should have made before he ruled:

1. THIS WOULD BE THE FOURTH ID SCHEME, not the second. Closed beads show hex -> sequential (seeds-e05, seeds-46e) -> base36 hash (seeds-mlj, which GRANDFATHERED the sequential ids). The corpus still carries both shapes today: seeds-183 alongside seeds-sdhc. A previous migration deliberately chose to leave it mixed.

2. THE ID SCHEME IS ALREADY UNDER OPEN DELIBERATION. seeds-32ai is still captured: "Should seed IDs be topic slugs rather than base36 hashes? Seeds outlive beads, so the inherited scheme may be the wrong trade." Changing the separator now either pre-empts that question or guarantees a fifth migration if slugs win.

3. THE EVIDENCE WAS THINNER THAN THE BAR THIS SESSION HELD EVERYWHERE ELSE. suggest was retired on ~15 uses across 5 sessions. The git oracle was refused without a demonstrated need. export was made to stop claiming a dependency it did not have. The evidence here was: an agent got confused once, and @aguynamedryan said it would "probably help me as well".

4. THE CONFUSION HAD A KNOWN, DIFFERENT CAUSE. The rejection that started this was a STALE .beads/issues.jsonl, filed as the stale-bead-ref bug. The id collision made the error message confusing; it did not cause the error.

5. IT STACKS A SECOND IDENTITY MIGRATION ON A STORAGE MIGRATION THAT IS HOURS OLD and untested on the other 14 repos. If something is wrong with the first, the second makes diagnosis harder.

THE PATH FORWARD: fix the stale-bead-ref bug, then resolve seeds-32ai deliberately so separator AND slug-vs-hash are decided together, then migrate ids ONCE, after 0.7 has been test-driven. The now-is-cheapest argument for doing it immediately is real but it is not worth a fourth scheme chosen in isolation.

title: Two format rules have no check in any tier: a resolution on a non-terminal seed, and non-canonical bytes
description:
Surfaced by the agent that built the smells tier (seeds-4co.4), which noted both in code and left them unimplemented because neither was in its acceptance criteria.

1. docs/storage-format.md section 3 says a 'resolution' on a non-terminal seed is a SMELL rather than a violation. Nothing checks it.
2. check.py's own docstring assigns the non-canonical-bytes case to smells -- a file whose bytes differ from what render_seed_file would emit. seedfile.py deliberately exports render_seed_file so this comparison can be made without writing. Nothing checks it.

Both matter more after conversion than before: byte-canonicality is what the converter's idempotence rests on, and a file hand-edited to a non-canonical shape is the thing that would make a later 'seeds convert' produce a spurious diff.

Judge the standing count before shipping either. The smells tier currently reports 32 on 308 records (25 empty-body, 7 duplicate-body), which is readable; a rule that adds hundreds would need rethinking, since the tier's whole credibility is its signal-to-noise on a healthy corpus.
acceptance_criteria: 'seeds check --smells' reports a seed carrying a resolution while its status is non-terminal, and a seed file whose bytes differ from render_seed_file's canonical output. Both are smells, never violations. A test pins each, and the standing smell count on the real 308-record corpus is reported in the bead so the tier's credibility can be judged.
notes:
PROMOTE ABOVE P3 — the non-canonical-bytes smell turns out to be a real defence, not tidiness. Within minutes of converting the live store (2026-09-01), ruff 0.16 tried to reformat a Python code block inside .seeds/seeds/seeds-154.md; its file count went 65 -> 385 the moment the tree landed. Excluding ruff is done, but every future repo-wide tool (prettier, markdownlint, a spell-checker) needs the same exclusion and nothing enforces that. A byte-canonicality check is the POSITIVE assertion that catches 'some tool rewrote a seed' whatever the tool was, instead of a growing exclusion list nobody maintains. It also protects seeds convert's idempotence, which a reformatted body silently breaks. See seeds-dv6r.
SCOPE EXTENDED (@aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01): add a THIRD thing, and it is the one he asked for — preemptively detect tool config files and assert they exclude .seeds/. Scan for the configs that exist (pyproject [tool.ruff], .prettierrc*, .markdownlint*, cspell.json, .editorconfig, and whatever else a repo has acquired) and fail when one does not exclude the seed store. Two layers, deliberately: this catches the tools we can name, and the canonical-bytes check catches whatever tool nobody predicted. Motivated by seeds-dv6r — ruff reached into the store within minutes of conversion.
DESIGN PICKS (2-way, code-only; ruled by the bead's own ambiguity rule):
1. The tool-config assertion (part 3) lands in SMELLS, not violations. Its fix
   lives in another tool's config file, so a fresh clone or a newly added dev
   tool could fail a commit that touched no seed — the shape that teaches
   people to bypass the hook.
2. "Excludes the store" is decided by whether the tool's config (parsed
   [tool.X] table for pyproject, plain text otherwise) or its companion ignore
   file (.prettierignore, .markdownlintignore, .cspellignore) names ".seeds" at
   all — not by parsing five dialects' exclude semantics. A second parser per
   tool is five more things that can be silently wrong; non-canonical-bytes is
   the backstop that makes the looseness affordable.

MEASURED LIMIT OF non-canonical-bytes — report this rather than over-trust it.
The comparison is the file against render_seed_file(what the file NOW says), so
it catches rewrites of the SERIALIZATION (extra trailing newline, blank lines
around the body, reordered frontmatter keys, re-encoded scalars) but NOT a
rewrite of the body's own text that leaves the layout canonical. ruff 0.16
reformatting a Python block inside a markdown body is exactly that blind spot,
and so is trimming trailing whitespace off a body line. Both are pinned by
tests (test_a_body_rewritten_within_canonical_layout_is_NOT_caught). The body
half belongs to --against-git, which compares the body field itself; a possible
follow-up is "body differs from HEAD while updated_at did not", which would
catch it exactly — deliberately NOT built here as it is another tier and
outside this bead.
CRLF and a BOM never reach this rule: the reader refuses both, so they stay
violations and are not double-counted.

STANDING SMELL COUNT on the real 309-file corpus: 32 before, 32 after
(25 empty-body, 7 duplicate-body). All three new rules score ZERO:
non-canonical-bytes 0/309, resolution-on-non-terminal 0/309,
tool-config-includes-store 0 (ruff is the only repo-wide tool configured here
and it carries extend-exclude = [".seeds/"]). Positive control run on a copy of
the real pyproject.toml with that line removed: the rule fires and names ruff,
so the silence is exclusion, not blindness.
close_reason: three smells added - resolution-on-non-terminal, non-canonical-bytes, and tool-config-includes-store; standing count on the real corpus unchanged at 32, with a positive control proving the tool-config zero is exclusion rather than blindness

title: Git-history repair oracle for the converter: recover fields both live stores got wrong together
description:
The converter (seeds-4co.6) deliberately does NOT mine git history, and @aguynamedryan accepted that decline on 2026-08-31, filing it here rather than closing the question.

The agent's reasoning, which is sound: mining git was in the bead description but not the acceptance criteria, and an AUTOMATIC repair from git is itself an auto-resolution of an ambiguity -- exactly what the four-way divergence design refuses to do for forks. seeds check's title tier already names seeds-wurl-shaped damage and points at git log -p as the remediation.

Why it is still worth having: seeds-wurl proved both live stores can agree and BOTH be wrong. 83 of 306 titles were replaced with a scratchpad path in 4144e8f, identically in DB and JSONL, and every divergence check was correctly green for three days. Git was the only source holding the truth. The storage plan called this load-bearing for exactly that reason.

The shape that resolves the tension: REPORT, never auto-apply. A verb that reads the ~113 commits touching .seeds/seeds.jsonl, reconstructs each seed's field history, and surfaces 'this field's current value in both stores differs from every value it held before commit X' as a finding a human rules on. That is detection, which is this project's settled enforcement strategy, rather than repair, which is the auto-resolution the converter rightly refuses.

Measured feasibility (2026-08-31): materializing the JSONL at each commit and pulling one record by id walks all 113 commits in 1.3s, and produces a clean per-seed revision list with real dates and authors.

NOT in the 0.7 critical path. The corpus is currently clean -- nothing needs repairing today.

Source: seeds-wurl, seeds-sdhc.1, seeds-sdhc.5, seeds-bp0s
acceptance_criteria: Given a corpus where DB and JSONL agree on a field but git history holds a different earlier value, the tool reports the discrepancy, names the commit the earlier value came from, and does NOT auto-apply it. Reproduces the seeds-wurl shape (83 titles replaced by a scratchpad path in 4144e8f, correct values in 63a47ca) from this repo's real history.
notes:
RESCOPED (@aguynamedryan asked whether the oracle is permanent or conversion-only, 2026-09-01): it is CONVERSION-ERA, and should be built as a ONE-TIME AUDIT rather than a standing verb. Reasoning: the oracle's job is 'two stores agree and are both wrong, so git is the third opinion'. After conversion there is exactly one store, so that shape is structurally impossible. The post-conversion equivalents already exist — 'seeds check --against-git' catches a mass rewrite, and 'seeds history' reads any single seed's real past. What remains genuinely unanswered is narrower: did any PRE-conversion corruption get baked into the converted tree? That is a one-time question per repo, answered by reading the JSONL history against the converted files, and it stops being askable once a repo's pre-conversion history is far enough behind to be irrelevant.
RULED (@aguynamedryan, 2026-09-01): run it ONCE as a script, report per repo, ship nothing. Then close.

The bead was already rescoped from a standing verb to a conversion-era audit. This narrows it further: do not build a command. The question it answers - is there pre-conversion corruption baked into any converted tree? - is asked once per repo and then stops being askable, and the coverage that overtook it is real. check --against-git catches the wurl sweep shape (its own help says so), the plausibility tier reports zero violations across all 11 convertible repos, and every conversion is round-trip verified field-by-field against the union input.

So: a one-off script comparing each converted tree against its .seeds/seeds.jsonl git history, a written report of what it found per repo, and then close the bead with the finding. If it finds nothing, that IS the result and it is worth having asked - the alternative is assuming.
RAN (2026-09-01, agent). scripts/conversion_audit.py — a one-off, per the
ruling: no verb, no just recipe, no docs. It walks each repo's
.seeds/seeds.jsonl git history with seeds.githistory (no third git walker),
materializes the corpus at every commit, and compares it against what the
store holds today — seed files for the one converted repo, the working JSONL
for the rest.

RESULT: NOTHING FOUND. 12 of 15 stores audited, 0 corrupt. No implausible
value in any current store; no mass sweep of implausible values survived into
any store; no body moved with updated_at frozen anywhere in 481 commits of
JSONL history; no body that history holds is empty now.

Not auditable, and why: agent_assessor, beads, mani. All three have a
.seeds/seeds.db and no .seeds/seeds.jsonl ever committed, so there is no
history to be the third opinion. Nothing to convert-and-compare either — the
question is unanswerable for them by any method, not merely unanswered.

POSITIVE CONTROL PASSED. In this repo the audit sees 4144e8f as a title sweep
of 87/305 seeds (29%) of which 83 are implausible-by-the-plausibility-tier,
names its subject, and reports REPAIRED because none of the swept values are
in the converted tree — 1afc51c put them back before conversion. So the shape
is visible in history even though the present is correct, which is what makes
the twelve CLEANs mean something.

WHAT THE CLEANS DO AND DO NOT COVER. Two signatures are scored as findings:
an implausible value the store holds now, and a sweep of implausible values
that survived. Everything else is reported as CONTEXT with its commit subject
— 21 mass sweeps across the corpus, all of plausible values (attribution
passes, bulk resolves, transcript ingests, three prefix renames that show as
whole-corpus deletions). No automatic rule separates a legitimate bulk edit
from a corrupting one, and inventing a threshold that did would be the
green-while-broken inversion in the other direction. A body quietly corrupted
into plausible-looking prose is NOT detectable by this or any automatic
method; that is the honest boundary of the answer.

The detectors are proven rather than assumed: `--self-check` fires all four
on hand-built input with hand-computed answers, including two negative
controls (9-of-40 stays under threshold; a stamped edit is not a quiet
rewrite). Three of the four returned zero on the real corpus, so a detector
that could not fire would have been indistinguishable from a clean corpus.

Logs (gitignored, local to titan): claude_stuff/conversion-audit-*.log.
CORRECTION to the note above: the JSONL history walked is 670 commits across
the 12 audited repos (163 code_collector, 247 code_set_catalog, 120 seeds, 43
ohdsi_supplemental_vocabs, 42 vocabulation, 14 vocabulary_formats, 12
habituate, 8 epc, 8 outcomesinsights.github.io, 5 oimnibus, 4 codesistant, 4
pman), not 481. Counted from git log; 481 was wrong.
close_reason: one-off audit run, nothing shipped: 12 of 15 stores audited across 670 commits of JSONL history, 0 corrupt; 3 (agent_assessor, beads, mani) are structurally unauditable because they have never committed a seeds.jsonl, so there is no history to be the third opinion; positive control passed - the audit sees 4144e8f's 87-seed title sweep in history and reports it REPAIRED, so the twelve CLEANs mean something

title: ruff target-version is py39 but the project requires >=3.10
description:
`pyproject.toml` has `[tool.ruff] target-version = "py39"` while `[project] requires-python = ">=3.10"`. Python 3.9 was dropped in v0.3.4 (end-of-life); the ruff setting was never updated.

## Why it matters

`target-version` tells ruff which syntax the codebase must remain compatible with. Pinned at `py39`, ruff's `UP` (pyupgrade) rules — which ARE enabled in `[tool.ruff.lint] select` — suppress every suggestion that would emit 3.10+ syntax. So the codebase is being held to a floor two versions below its actual one, and modernizations ruff would otherwise offer are invisible.

Harmless in the sense that nothing is broken. Wrong in the sense that the config states something untrue about the project.

## Expect this to cascade

Changing one line may surface a batch of `UP` findings — 3.10 brought `X | Y` union syntax, `match`, and parenthesized context managers, and `UP` will start proposing the union-syntax rewrites in particular. That is the actual work; the config edit is trivial.

Apply ruff's autofixes where they are safe and mechanical. If any suggested rewrite is NOT mechanical, or reduces clarity, leave it and say which — do not contort code to satisfy a lint rule. Note the codebase already uses `from __future__ import annotations` in places, which affects how annotation-related rules apply.
acceptance_criteria:
- `grep -n 'target-version' pyproject.toml` shows `py310`, matching `requires-python = ">=3.10"`.
- `uv run ruff check .` is clean at the new target.
- `uv run ruff format --check .` is clean.
- `uv run mypy src/` is clean (note `[tool.mypy] python_version` is separately set to 3.10 — confirm the two now agree).
- pytest passes on ALL FOUR supported versions, since the point is that 3.10 is the real floor: `for v in 3.10 3.11 3.12 3.13; do uv run --python $v --no-sync pytest -q || break; done`
- Any ruff suggestion deliberately NOT applied is listed in the bead notes with the reason.
close_reason: target-version now py310, matching requires-python and [tool.mypy] python_version. Surfaced UP035 (autofixed) and B905 in first_difference, where strict=False is correct because the bodies routinely differ in length; documented in the docstring. Verified across 3.10-3.13.

title: Enable hallucination checking for base36 IDs via a domain-term allowlist
description:
Hash-shaped references (`seeds-zq4x`) are currently invisible to hallucination checking. `find_id_refs` is called from `_validate_id_refs` with no `known_ids`, so `_is_id_ref` discards every non-numeric token before it is ever checked. An agent can cite a base36 ID that never existed and nothing notices — which is exactly the failure the check was built to catch, and base36 is the scheme every new ID uses (seeds-199).

Source: seeds-6hj5. **Depends on the bead-ID loading bead** — without it, enabling this flags all 16 legitimate bead references.

## The design (Ryan's, arrived at over three rounds of pushback — do not re-derive)

Check each candidate token against, in order:

1. **seed IDs** (exists today)
2. **bead IDs** (the prerequisite bead)
3. **a small allowlist of domain terms** (this bead)

Anything still unmatched is a hallucination — flag it.

The regex stays, but only to extract candidate tokens from free text. It performs no judgment; that was a red herring in the seed's earlier framing.

## Why an allowlist rather than a heuristic

"Cannot distinguish a hash from a word by shape" is true and does not matter, because you can enumerate the exceptions when there are eight of them. Measured across all 268 seeds — the complete set of `seeds-*` prose tokens in the project's entire history:

```
seeds-marketplace    seeds-cli       seeds-native    seeds-tool
seeds-generated      seeds-level     seeds-like      seeds-side
```

These are real domain vocabulary, not contrived: `seeds-marketplace` is the Claude Code plugin marketplace, `seeds-cli` is the PyPI name under consideration in seeds-95. Seed the allowlist with exactly these eight.

**Rejected alternative — do not implement:** a length/entropy heuristic (require a digit, reject dictionary words). An all-digit suffix is a valid hash and a 4-letter English word is valid base36, so it both misses and false-positives. seeds-6hj5 records this as a trap.

## Note: this makes the check STRICTER

Today hash-shaped hallucinations pass silently. After this they are caught. That is the point — but it means seeds whose bodies were written under the looser rule may now fail validation. Run the new check across the existing 268-seed database before shipping and confirm it reports zero unknowns; if it reports any, they are either real hallucinations worth fixing or allowlist entries worth adding. Record the outcome in the bead notes.

## Where the allowlist lives

Prefer a module-level constant with a comment explaining what it is and when to add to it — a future reader must understand these are prose, not IDs. Making it user-configurable is NOT required; revisit only if the list grows past ~20 entries. Maintenance is roughly one addition every few months, and the failure mode is a clear error naming exactly what to add.
acceptance_criteria:
- A reference to a nonexistent hash-shaped ID is now REJECTED: in a temp SEEDS_DIR, `seeds create -t "t" -c "see seeds-zq4x"` exits non-zero and names `seeds-zq4x`. (This currently succeeds — verify it fails after the change.)
- Every one of the 8 allowlisted terms is accepted: creating a seed whose body contains `seeds-marketplace`, `seeds-cli`, `seeds-native`, `seeds-tool`, `seeds-generated`, `seeds-level`, `seeds-like`, `seeds-side` succeeds without `--allow-unknown-refs`.
- Real bead references still pass (the prerequisite bead's behavior is not regressed): a body citing `seeds-230` succeeds.
- Real seed references still pass: a body citing an existing seed ID succeeds.
- Running the validator over all 268 existing seeds reports zero unknown references — script it, paste the output, and record any allowlist additions in the bead notes.
- `--allow-unknown-refs` still overrides everything.
- Tests cover: hallucinated hash rejected, allowlisted term accepted, real bead accepted, real seed accepted.
- `uv run pytest` green; `uv run ruff check .` clean; `uv run mypy src/` clean.
notes:
Pre-ship sweep of the real .seeds/seeds.jsonl (270 seeds, 100 beads, read-only: JSONL parsed directly, validation logic called in-process, no mutating commands).

RESULT: 16 distinct prefixed tokens resolved to neither a seed nor a bead. ZERO were hallucinations.

The 8 the bead measured were confirmed and seeded into PROSE_REF_ALLOWLIST: marketplace, cli, native, tool, generated, level, like, side.

The sweep found 5 MORE word-shaped prose terms the measurement missed (each occurs once, in seeds written after or outside the measured set). All are the same category as the original 8, so they were added to the allowlist, bringing it to 13 (bead threshold for revisiting is ~20):
  - experiment  (seeds-199: "`seeds-experiment`-style IDs")
  - recent      (seeds-87: the `seeds recent` primitive)
  - specific    (seeds-74.2.2: "a seeds-specific phrase")
  - sweep       (seeds-74.2.2: the proposed /seeds-sweep slash command)
  - whatever    (seeds-6hj5: placeholder inside a quoted design discussion)

3 residual tokens were deliberately NOT allowlisted, because they are ID-shaped, not prose -- design write-ups quoting a fabricated example ID. Allowlisting an ID-shaped token would blind the check to that ID forever, inverting the point of the list:
  - seeds-7.1  (seeds-140 content: "e.g., seeds-1, seeds-7.1") -- PRE-EXISTING. It is numeric, so today/main already flags it; the baseline sweep on main reports this same 1 hit. Not a regression from this bead.
  - seeds-k3n  (seeds-199 content: "a 3-4 char id like `seeds-k3n`") -- the ONLY new failure this bead introduces across the whole corpus.
  - seeds-8su  (seeds-199 RESOLUTION field) -- out of the validated surface entirely: create validates [title, content] and update validates [title, content, append]; no command validates resolution.

So the post-change sweep over the validated surface reports 2 unknowns, not 0: one pre-existing (seeds-7.1) and one new (seeds-k3n). Both are documentation prose quoting example IDs; the honest fix is in those two seed bodies (write them as placeholders, or use --allow-unknown-refs when next editing them), not in the allowlist. The seed bodies were NOT edited -- the sweep was required to be read-only.
Design picks not pinned by the bead:

1. find_id_refs -> find_id_ref_candidates. The bead says the regex "performs no judgment", and _validate_id_refs was its only production caller. Rather than add a second extractor and leave find_id_refs as dead-but-tested code, the function was renamed and its known_ids parameter dropped: it now returns every whole-word <prefix>-... token and the caller judges. _is_id_ref keeps its known_ids logic, still used by rewrite_id_refs / iter_id_ref_snippets on the prefix-rename path.

2. Allowlist stored as BARE SUFFIXES (frozenset {"cli", "native", ...}), not full "seeds-cli" tokens, so a project with any other prefix inherits the vocabulary. Verified: in a csc-prefixed temp store, "a csc-native workflow with csc-cli" is accepted while "csc-zq4x" is rejected. A test asserts no entry contains a hyphen, so a future prefixed entry (which would silently never match) fails loudly.

3. Error message now names the constant to add to: "If one is prose rather than an ID, add its suffix to PROSE_REF_ALLOWLIST in seeds/models.py."
close_reason: base36 refs now validated: seed IDs -> bead IDs -> 13-entry bare-suffix prose allowlist. Sweep of 270 seeds + 100 beads found 16 unmatched, zero hallucinations. AC predicted zero residuals; actual is 2 (seeds-7.1 pre-existing/numeric, seeds-k3n the one new hit) — both ID-shaped examples in prose, deliberately not allowlisted, decision recorded on seeds-6hj5.

title: Emit compact JSON from seeds suggest --json (no indent, tight separators)
description:
`seeds suggest --json` pretty-prints with `indent=2`, even though the flag's own help text reads **"Emit JSON for agent piping"**. The single place seeds pretty-prints JSON is the one place whose stated purpose is machine consumption. Make it compact.

Source: seeds-d773 (deliberation). Related: seeds-142.1 (originated `seeds suggest` and asked "JSON output mode for agent piping?"), seeds-137 / seeds-138 (output-economy family).

## Motivation

JSON emitted for an agent is JSON an LLM pays tokens to read. Indentation is pure overhead on that path. Measured on a real `seeds suggest` result: 406 bytes pretty vs 292 compact — **28.1% smaller**.

## Locked decisions — do NOT re-open

- **Always compact. No `--pretty` flag, no config option.** Ryan's call, verbatim: *"maybe we don't even need that. Maybe we just want it compacted at all times. And someone can just run it through JQ when they want a pretty printed version."* Rationale: `jq` is the universal pretty-printer and already installed everywhere we care about; a flag is surface area to document, test, and keep working in exchange for what one pipe already does.
- **Do NOT make it TTY-conditional** (compact when piped, pretty when interactive). This was considered and rejected: output that changes shape depending on whether stdout is a terminal is exactly what surprises someone debugging a pipeline, and it contradicts the "one predictable machine format" intent above.
- **Use `separators=(",", ":")`, not merely dropping `indent`.** Python's `json.dumps` keeps `", "` / `": "` padding by default. Measured: `indent=2` 599 bytes -> no-indent 453 -> tight separators 415. Dropping indent alone leaves ~8% on the table.

## Scope fence — exactly one line changes

`src/seeds/cli.py:472`, inside the `suggest` command:

```python
click.echo(_json.dumps(payload, indent=2))
```

becomes the tight-separator form. That is the whole production change.

**Do NOT touch these** (audited 2026-08-10, all four are correct as-is):
- `src/seeds/export.py:103` — the JSONL export. It uses default separators and is NOT maximally compact, and that is deliberate. Compacting it would rewrite every line of a git-tracked 520KB file (permanently muddying `git log -p` / `git blame` on the whole deliberation history) to save 1.8%. It is a sync artifact, not agent-facing output. seeds-d773 records this decision — do not "finish the job" here.
- `src/seeds/db.py:424,466` — tags serialized into SQLite. Internal storage; nothing reads it as text.
- `src/seeds/web.py` — its three Flask routes render HTML templates and emit no JSON at all.
- Any `json.loads` call site — those are reads, not output.

## Also update the help text

The `--json` flag's help currently reads `"Emit JSON for agent piping"`. Make it state the format is compact, so nobody is surprised or files this as a bug — e.g. `"Emit compact JSON for agent piping (pipe through jq to read it)"`.
acceptance_criteria:
- `uv run seeds suggest "nix" --json` output contains NO newline except a single trailing one: `uv run seeds suggest "nix" --json | wc -l` returns 1.
- Output contains no `", "` or `": "` separator padding: `uv run seeds suggest "nix" --json | grep -cE '", "|": "'` returns 0.
- Output is still valid JSON: `uv run seeds suggest "nix" --json | jq -e 'type == "array"'` exits 0.
- Field content is unchanged — same keys as before: `uv run seeds suggest "nix" --json | jq -e '.[0] | has("id") and has("title") and has("status") and has("tags") and has("snippet") and has("score")'` exits 0 (when there is at least one result).
- `grep -n 'indent=2' src/seeds/cli.py` returns no match.
- `.seeds/seeds.jsonl` is byte-identical to before the change (`git diff --stat .seeds/seeds.jsonl` shows nothing beyond ordinary seed edits) — the export was NOT touched.
- `grep -c 'compact' src/seeds/cli.py` >= 1 (the --json help text mentions the format).
- A test covers the compact shape so it cannot silently regress to pretty-printing.
- Full suite green: `uv run pytest`.
close_reason: suggest --json now emits compact JSON (separators=(',',':')); 21% smaller on a live query; regression test verified to fail against indent=2

title: Flaky test: test_rename_prefix_no_rewrite_bodies fails intermittently under full-suite runs
description:
`tests/test_cli.py::TestRenamePrefixCommand::test_rename_prefix_no_rewrite_bodies` fails intermittently. Observed once during a pre-commit hook run on main; did NOT reproduce on a subsequent full-suite run (433 passed) or on 5/5 isolated runs of the test alone.

## Observed failure

```
    result = cli_runner.invoke(main, ["show", hub_id])
    # Reference is now stale — the seeds-1 in body wasn't rewritten.
>   assert "see seeds-1" in result.output
E   assert 'see seeds-1' in "Error: Seed 'seeds-060' not found.\n"
E    +  where "Error: Seed 'seeds-060' not found.\n" = <Result SystemExit(1)>
tests/test_cli.py:281
```

## Likely cause

The test hardcodes a seed at id `seeds-1`, then CLI-creates a second ("hub") whose id comes from `next_id()`. Since the switch to base36 hash IDs (seeds-tek / seeds-mlj, grandfathering sequential), the generated id varies per run — here it was `seeds-060`.

The assertion depends on `show hub_id` still resolving AFTER `rename-prefix demo` has run. That only holds if `show` can still resolve the pre-rename id. So the test is probably sensitive to which id shape `next_id()` produces — i.e. whether the generated id looks sequential (grandfathered path) or base36-hash (new path), and whether the rename/lookup logic treats those differently.

That would make this not merely a flaky test but a **real inconsistency in `rename-prefix` / `show` id resolution across the two id shapes** — worth determining which before "fixing the test."

## Do NOT

- Do not paper over it by loosening the assertion or adding a retry. Determine first whether the flake is in the test's assumption or in `rename-prefix`/`show` behavior. If it's the latter, this bead becomes a production bug and the test is correct as written.

## Reproduction hint

Isolated runs pass. Reproduce by running the full suite repeatedly, or seed `next_id()` deterministically to force a base36-hash id (vs a grandfathered sequential one) and run the test under each.
acceptance_criteria:
- Root cause identified and stated in the bead notes: test-assumption bug vs. real `rename-prefix`/`show` id-resolution inconsistency.
- A test exists that deterministically exercises BOTH id shapes (grandfathered sequential and base36 hash) through `rename-prefix` followed by `show`.
- `uv run pytest` passes 20 consecutive full-suite runs (`for i in $(seq 20); do uv run pytest -q || break; done`).
- If a production bug was found, the fix is in src/ and not only in tests/.
notes:
DIRECTION FROM RYAN (2026-07-26): "fix test and understand we're doing base36 going forward."

Base36 hash IDs are the standard for all NEW ids (resolved in seeds-199, shipped via seeds-tek + seeds-mlj). Sequential ids are grandfathered legacy, not a co-equal scheme — do not add new machinery to keep sequential generation alive.

BUT both shapes genuinely coexist in real databases and must both keep working. This very repo proves it: sequential ids (seeds-95, seeds-112, seeds-154) sit alongside base36 hash ids (seeds-gf69, seeds-0y4, seeds-80g) in the same .seeds database. So `rename-prefix` and `show` must resolve BOTH correctly — the acceptance criterion covering both shapes stands.

Framing: treat base36 as the normal path and sequential as legacy data that must not break. If the root cause turns out to be that `rename-prefix`/`show` mishandles one shape, fix the production code — do not loosen the test.
ROOT CAUSE (2026-07-26): production bug in rename-prefix, not just a bad test assumption.

Database.rename_prefix decided which IDs belonged to the old prefix with a
numeric-only shape test written back when every ID was sequential:

    try:
        int(top[len(old_lead):])   # 'seeds-7' -> 7
    except ValueError:
        continue                    # skipped

A base36 hash suffix is drawn from [0-9a-z], so ~2% of length-3 hashes are
all digits. 'seeds-060' therefore parsed as a number and WAS renamed, while
'seeds-k3n7' was not. Same ID shape, opposite outcome, decided by the random
content of the hash — that is the whole flake. The observed failure ('Error:
Seed seeds-060 not found') was the hub seed getting renamed to demo-060 and
'show seeds-060' then missing it; the test passed on every run where the
minted hash happened to contain a letter.

Consequences beyond the flake: 'seeds rename-prefix demo' on a real database
left it in a split-prefix state — demo-1 and demo-060 renamed, seeds-k3n7
stranded — while get_prefix() reported 'demo', so new IDs minted as demo-*
against mostly seeds-* data. That contradicts the command's own contract
('rewrite all seed IDs to use it'). This repo would hit it today: seeds-95
and seeds-112 sit alongside seeds-gf69 and seeds-0y4.

FIX (src/, per the bead): both schemes rename, deterministically.
- idgen.is_hash_suffix(suffix, min_len, max_len): base36 chars within the
  configured adaptive-length window. New helper, no new ID generation.
- rename_prefix now matches suffix.isdigit() (grandfathered sequential, any
  length) OR is_hash_suffix(...) (base36, the standard). 'seeds-experiment'
  still isn't renamed — 10 chars exceeds max_hash_length, so the original
  guard's purpose is preserved.
- Body refs had the same numeric-only assumption (_id_ref_pattern matched
  \\d+ only). Renaming hash IDs without this would strand every mention of
  them, so the pattern now matches base36 and rewrite_id_refs/find_id_refs/
  iter_id_ref_snippets take a known_ids set: numeric refs rewrite
  unconditionally (preserves refs to deleted seeds), hash-shaped refs only
  when they name a real seed. Nothing can tell 'seeds-related' from a hash
  by shape, so database membership is the only sound test.

DESIGN PICK (2-way, documented): make rename-prefix rename BOTH shapes rather
than deterministically skip hash IDs. Skipping is unsound (all-digit hashes
are indistinguishable from sequential IDs) and would make rename-prefix a
near no-op now that base36 is the standard. Consequence: the two CLI tests
that asserted a hash-ID seed survives rename-prefix encoded the bug; they now
assert the seed is renamed and that 'show' resolves the new ID. No assertion
was loosened — the stale-body-ref assertion is preserved verbatim.

VERIFICATION: 20/20 consecutive full-suite runs green (457 passed each). Both
new deterministic tests fail against pre-fix src (verified by stashing the
src changes), so they are real regression tests rather than the flake's luck.
close_reason: root cause was a production bug: rename_prefix used a numeric-only int() test, renaming all-digit base36 hashes but skipping alphanumeric ones; now matches both schemes, body-ref rewriting gated on known_ids

title: (Stretch) Add seeds:seeds-to-beads prompt-macro skill to the seeds plugin
description:
Optional follow-on to the feedback-skill spike. Once the install mechanism is proven (seeds-dn7 passes), adding a second prompt-macro skill is a small repeat.

Reference deliberation: seeds-152.4 (this skill's design rationale and resolution of the workflow-engine-vs-macro tension).

This bead is stretch scope. Only do it if seeds-dn7 has passed and there's time. If the prompt-macro framing turns out to be insufficient in practice, file a new seed rather than expanding scope here.

## File to create

src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/skills/seeds-to-beads/SKILL.md

## Exact content

```markdown
---
name: seeds-to-beads
description: Use when the user has reached agreement on a feature after a deliberation captured in seeds, and wants the relevant seeds turned into a set of beads (tasks) executable by a Sonnet-based agent.
---

# Seeds → beads conversion

The user has deliberated a feature using seeds and now wants the agreed scope handed off as beads for execution by a Sonnet-based agent. Convert the relevant seeds into a set of beads following these principles:

- Separate actionable scope (decisions, agreed paths) from context (concerns, observations, refinements). Beads represent work; seeds carry the deliberation.
- Decompose into small, self-contained beads. Each bead should be doable in one focused effort.
- Pre-write content. If a bead requires a file with specific content, include the content verbatim in the bead description so the executing agent doesn't have to re-design.
- Acceptance criteria must be mechanically checkable (file exists, command exits 0, output contains string X).
- Set explicit dependencies between beads.
- Cite seed IDs for deliberation context the executing agent might need.
- After creating beads, land the plane: commit unstaged work into a clean tree.

Do this conversion once when invoked. Do not adopt the conversion behavior as a default for subsequent turns.
```

## Plugin version bump

Bump the version in both manifest files (src/seeds/plugin/.claude-plugin/marketplace.json and src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/.claude-plugin/plugin.json) from 0.1.0 to 0.2.0 so `claude plugin update` recognizes the change.
acceptance_criteria:
1. File exists: src/seeds/plugin/claude-plugin/skills/seeds-to-beads/SKILL.md
2. File contains the YAML frontmatter with `name: seeds-to-beads`
3. File contains the load-bearing principles (separation of action vs context, content templates, mechanical acceptance criteria, dependencies, seed IDs, land-the-plane)
4. File contains the "do this once when invoked" self-scope constraint (per seeds-151.2 and seeds-152.4)
5. Both manifest files have version bumped from 0.1.0 to 0.2.0
6. Running `seeds skills install` (or update) picks up the new skill
7. File length under 30 lines
close_reason: Added seeds-to-beads SKILL.md + bumped plugin manifests to 0.2.0

title: Tighten conn typing on Database migration helpers
description:
The \`_migrate_add_resolution\` / \`_migrate_add_config\` (and now \`_apply_body_id_rewrites\`) methods use \`conn = self._conn\` and then call \`conn.execute(...)\` without narrowing the Optional[Connection] type. Pre-existing pattern; mypy flags 7 errors.

Fix: route through \`self._get_conn()\` so the type narrows, or add an explicit assertion. The runtime behavior is fine — these methods are only called after \`_get_conn\` populated \`self._conn\` — but the type hint should reflect that.

## Acceptance
- \`uv run mypy src/seeds/\` reports 0 errors in db.py
- All 285+ tests still pass
- No runtime behavior change
close_reason: Pulled conn out as method parameter on _migrate_add_resolution/_migrate_add_config; annotated get_config return. mypy now clean: 0 errors in 7 source files.
